stories.Headline: SpaceX Announces Massive $74 Billion Investment To Build Two AI Supercomputing Campuses In Texas And Arizona
stories.Summary:
SpaceX announced on Thursday, November 12, 2026, that it plans to invest more than $74 billion in two artificial intelligence supercomputing campuses, one in Texas and one in Arizona. The company issued a statement outlining the two projects and the jobs they are expected to create. The Texas facility is priced at more than $24 billion and sits in the Rio Grande Valley near the company's Starbase rocket launch site. The Arizona campus is priced at roughly $50 billion and would be built in Cochise County. The company said the plans would expand its computing infrastructure, and each campus relies on its own separate power arrangement.

The Texas development covers about 444 acres between Boca Chica Boulevard and the Port of Brownsville, near the city's landfill. The $24 billion figure covers only the initial phases and leaves room for future expansion. The Texas project has already produced more than 3,000 construction jobs and is expected to support more than 500 permanent positions. The Arizona campus would occupy about 747 acres near Willcox Playa, roughly 80 miles east of Tucson, and could scale up to 6 gigawatts at full buildout. It is expected to create about 5,500 construction jobs and 1,000 permanent jobs, with a proposed $3.6 billion for electrical infrastructure and a 24-gigawatt-hour battery storage system.

SpaceX is the party behind both projects, and it says the Starbase facility will generate its own electricity without drawing from the public grid. A Starbase public hearing notice names Space Exploration Technologies Corp. as the owner and applicant for the gas-fired power plant and supercomputing facility. In Arizona, the company says it is working with local electric cooperatives and intends to use existing renewable energy resources. It also says the Arizona campus will use dry-cooling technology with no planned industrial groundwater consumption. SpaceX says the project could cut electricity bills for cooperative members by as much as 20 percent, and that the Texas facility will help train AI systems for medical research, emergency response, manufacturing and national security.

The Texas site has drawn opposition from environmental advocates, and the South Texas Environmental Justice Network organized a protest. The group argues the new facilities would pollute the air, use up water and raise energy bills for residents. In Arizona, a petition opposing the campus has gathered about 2,400 signatures, and residents in both states have raised concerns about environmental impact. Brownsville said it stands by its deal with SpaceX and stressed the importance of securing the $220 million in water funding. The city also said it remains committed to evaluating concerns and protecting water resources, and the Arizona and Texas communities are the ones most directly affected.

Brownsville voted earlier this year to remove the land from its city boundaries at SpaceX's request, in exchange for up to $220 million toward its water and wastewater infrastructure. That money is expected to add about 20 million gallons of daily water capacity. The annexation placed the land outside a 90-day moratorium on data center applications that took effect in Brownsville on November 5. About three-quarters of Brownsville's primary water supply comes from two Rio Grande reservoirs, both of which have faced critically low levels. SpaceX said relying on public financing for the gap would have cost ratepayers $370 million over 25 years, including interest.

The Starbase City Commission is scheduled to consider a property tax abatement and a related economic development agreement for the Texas project at a hearing on December 9. The Arizona campus remains subject to approval by Cochise County and other local authorities. Across Texas, data center developers are expected to face stronger headwinds under Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned on halting new approvals until the state adopts additional rules. Those rules would cover electricity costs, water use and the role of local communities. One account says about 90 percent of the spending will not happen without full approval and permits, and the articles do not say whether any of these approvals will be granted.

stories.Headline: Adobe, Google expand AI partnership across creative, productivity tools
stories.Summary:
Adobe and Google expanded their strategic AI partnership on November 14, 2026, to integrate advanced models into creative tools. This collaboration brings Google AI models into Adobe software and extends Adobe tools across the Google productivity ecosystem. Adobe also unveiled new AI agents and features at the Adobe MAX 2026 conference in Miami. This annual creative event opened on October 10 and showcased the evolution of the Firefly generative app. The updates aim to turn Firefly into a comprehensive AI creative studio for all digital creators.

Google Gemini models will power Acrobat, allowing users to edit PDFs via conversational prompts through Google Workspace, Drive, and Gmail. Adobe Firefly, Photoshop, Premiere, and Express will integrate Google image and video models, including Gemini Omni, Veo, and Nano Banana. Firefly now supports 36 models, including ByteDance's Dreamina and Seedance 2.5, Runway's Gen-4.5, Kuaishou's Kling 4.0, and OpenAI's GPT. Adobe also partnered with Disney for custom Firefly Foundry models and Microsoft for Arm-based Windows PCs and Microsoft Photos. New tools include Firefly Design in beta, Firefly Builder in private beta, and the CX Enterprise Coworker in GenStudio.

Forrest Key, vice president for Firefly and agentic AI, stated the company wants to help everyone create digital content. He described Firefly as the best platform for both new creators and professionals to build their digital work. Deepa Subramaniam, vice president of product marketing for Creative Cloud, said updates provide professionals with precision, control, and flexibility. She noted that these new tools allow professionals to focus on the decisions that shape their own creative work. The companies are also exploring custom Google image models for Photoshop to enable near-real-time editing through text prompts.

Users of Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Lightroom are affected by these updates, including new lighting and color tools. Premiere mobile users gain natural-language editing and licensed music from UMG and WMG for personal, non-commercial video projects. Designers can use Firefly Design to combine illustration, animation, and 3D tools on a single canvas for efficiency. Marketing teams can now use the Ideation Space in Workfront to build campaign strategies and briefs using AI. Business users can coordinate agents and workflows across planning and activation using the new CX Enterprise Coworker interface.

Adobe's multi-model strategy allows users to work with different AI models alongside professional editing tools in the Creative Cloud. Firefly was developed as a generative AI app offering image and video generation, editing, and now agent-based workflow tools. The company introduced a plan mode for reviewing agent plans and a model picker for selecting specific AI models. Always-on agents are being previewed to handle repetitive background tasks like organizing assets and checking content quality. Adobe also developed Firefly Graph in beta for users who want to build repeatable and efficient creative workflows.

Next, Adobe will expand integrations with Gemini and Gemini Enterprise to bring Acrobat and creative tools into those platforms. The company is rolling out beta features like Generative Remove in Premiere and real-time co-editing in InDesign. Local MCP integrations are being previewed to allow third-party agents to edit native project files while keeping layers editable. Adobe continues to test Firefly Builder for turning spoken descriptions into prototypes for websites and mobile apps without coding. The articles leave open how the custom Google models for Photoshop will perform in real-time text-to-image editing.

stories.Headline: UPDATE: California teachers union calls for 3-year pause on AI in K-8 classrooms
stories.Summary:
The California Federation of Teachers sent a letter on Wednesday urging Gov. Gavin Newsom to pause artificial intelligence in K-8 public school classrooms, The Sacramento Bee reported. The union asked for a three-year pause, citing concerns that schools are adopting AI tools without adequate protections for students and educators. The call followed Newsom's September executive order directing state agencies to develop AI safety regulations, including a potential "kill switch" for certain AI programs during emergencies. The union represents 120,000 teachers from preschool to college, according to EdSource. The letter was sent to the outgoing California governor before his term ends in January.

The union urged Newsom to issue an executive order pausing AI use in classrooms before January. The letter cited an MIT study linking ChatGPT use to weaker brain connectivity while writing essays. It also cited research from the Wharton Healthcare Analytics Lab that found students who used GPT-4 scored 17% lower on a math test than students who hadn't used it. The union said educators need more time to be prepared to supervise AI use. The release said students may struggle to tell which tools are safe or harmful.

CFT President Jeff Freitas said in a statement that students' brain development shouldn't be monetized for billionaire profit. Freitas said this is a public health and safety emergency and that leaders need to treat it as one and act now. The union warned that unregulated AI could harm students' development and limit teachers' control over instruction. The letter said the explosion of the AI industry is more than just market growth. The letter said the infusion of AI in education is happening at an ever-accelerating pace, and each week more alarming examples emerge of AI products leaking student data, failing to accurately complete the work they were designed for, costing teachers and staff invaluable time, and with dubious educational benefits for students.

The union said educators aren't prepared to supervise AI use. The release said advocacy groups have urged Newsom to impose stronger accountability and protections as he has largely embraced AI's growth in California throughout his governorship. The letter asked Newsom to pause the AI usage and provide schools time to address those emerging concerns. The union represents 120,000 educators and faculty, according to the news release. The call was reported by The Sacramento Bee and distributed by Tribune Content Agency.

Newsom's September executive order directed state agencies to develop AI safety regulations, including a potential "kill switch" for certain AI programs during emergencies. The union sent a letter to the outgoing California governor warning that unregulated AI could harm students' development and limit teachers' control over instruction. The letter cited an MIT study linking ChatGPT use to weaker brain connectivity during essay writing. The letter cited Wharton Healthcare Analytics Lab research that found students who used GPT-4 scored 17 percent lower on a later unassisted math test than students who hadn't used it. The union said educators need more time to be prepared to supervise AI use.

The union urged Newsom to issue an executive order pausing AI use in classrooms before his term ends in January. The articles do not say whether Newsom has responded to the letter or the request. The articles do not say when the three-year pause would begin or end. The articles do not name the specific AI tools or programs that would be covered beyond ChatGPT and GPT-4. The articles do not say what happens if Newsom does not act before his term ends.

stories.Headline: Is AI involved in today's FAA nationwide ground stop?
stories.Summary:
Federal officials are investigating whether a newly announced artificial intelligence program may have played a role in the telecommunications issue that prompted a nationwide ground stop at U.S. airports on Friday, November 13, 2026. The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon for just the second time since the September 11, 2001, attacks. The FAA ordered the nationwide ground stop for departing flights due to safety concerns, and Houston airports were impacted. The FAA said technicians are investigating the communications failure affecting air traffic control centers nationwide. The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop that had blocked takeoffs for hours.

The FAA began its initial rollout of the new artificial intelligence system called Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) in September, with plans to expand its use. The Transportation Department describes SMART as an advanced air traffic management tool designed to use real-time information, including weather conditions, airport congestion and flight paths, to help adjust and streamline routes for pilots. The system is designed to improve efficiency and reduce delays. According to information presented during the news conference, FAA specialists are expected to remain involved in operating and overseeing the system during its rollout. The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the September 11, 2001, attacks.

During a news conference in Washington, D.C., Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the Department of Homeland Security is working with other federal agencies to determine whether the FAA's new AI technology contributed to the disruption. Mullin stressed that there is no threat to the public, describing the situation as a telecommunications issue. Mullin said, "That's part of something that obviously through CISA at DHS we're taking a look," and "We're working with our counterparts throughout all agencies." Mullin said federal officials are examining whether the new technology had any connection to Friday's telecommunications disruption, though officials have not established that the AI system caused the problem. Mullin attributed the problem to a telecommunications outage and said there was no indication the communications failure was related to a cyberattack.

Air Space Intelligence, the AI tech startup that is a vendor for the FAA on its new SMART system for air traffic control, said its software didn't cause today's nationwide ground stop. NBC News' Brian Cheung and Jared Perlo reported on the AI system and its new implementation by the FAA. The consequences were profound, disrupting potentially thousands of planned flights through at least late Friday night. Travelers were stranded at Sky Harbor after the FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop. Travelers were stranded at Raleigh-Durham airport, and frustrated Chicago travelers sought answers on checked bags amid the nationwide ground stop.

The FAA grounded all flights nationwide Friday afternoon as officials cited "extraordinary circumstances" caused by communications problems at regional air traffic control centers. The nation's top homeland security official attributed the problem to a telecommunications outage. The nationwide ground stop raised questions about AI regulation. White House officials asked for $50 billion after the ground stop was lifted. Secretary Duffy detailed the timeline of the ground stop and demanded more FAA funding.

The FAA lifted the nationwide ground stop as thousands of flights were canceled. Secretary Duffy called on Congress to fund improvements to the air system. Secretary Duffy said data inconsistencies triggered the FAA ground stop. The DHS said the nationwide ground stop was not a cyberattack, saying "We are built to handle crisis like this." The articles leave open whether the AI system caused the problem, as officials have not established that connection.

stories.Headline: Your phone knows you're at the doctor, and data brokers do, too — then profit from it
stories.Summary:
Chris McQueen finished leukemia treatment a year and a half ago, but ads for fake cures never stopped appearing on his mobile phone. Juice cleanses to cure cancer, natural cancer treatments, and clinics in Mexico promising full recovery with little chemotherapy appeared during routine oncologist visits and monthly bloodwork. McQueen and others have taken to social media to vent about data brokers tracking their whereabouts via smartphone location data. The brokers connect that data with other data gathered about them and draw inferences about their health struggles. They sell to companies hawking unproven treatments, and McQueen, who lives in San Diego, said it makes him feel sick to his stomach.

More than 92% of patients in a 2022 American Medical Association survey said they believed their health data should not be available for purchase. Location data emitted from mobile phones in a hospital, an abortion clinic, or an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting in a church basement is not covered by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, better known as HIPAA. California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat, on Sept. 27 vetoed a bill that would have blocked the sale and sharing of location and other sensitive personal data, saying it went a step too far. A recent Stanford University study showed that only 9% of data brokers are adhering to an existing California privacy law that gives consumers the right to delete their data, correct personal information, and learn what personal records the business is selling. In January, Consumer Reports released model legislation giving state lawmakers a framework to ban or limit the sale of geolocation data, which uses GPS to identify a person's movements in real time.

Eric Ellsworth, director of health policy and innovation at the Center for the Study of Services, said data brokers typically are just hoovering up data from the open web and then buying it from anybody. F. Mario Trujillo, senior staff attorney at the Electronic Frontier Foundation, said data brokers and advertisers argue that location data itself is not sensitive data, but that location data is sensitive and it is the comprehensive collection of location data that reveals sensitive things. Jim Potter, executive director of 4As Health, a subsidiary of the American Association of Advertising Agencies, said a national privacy law should protect consumers from harmful or unexpected uses of data without preventing businesses from providing the services consumers request and expect. Potter said that balance is especially important in advertising, which is not merely a business model but a key part of the modern economy. Microsoft spokesperson Paige Fisher said the company has long believed that people should not have to give up their privacy simply because they use modern technology.

Connecticut, Delaware, Maryland, New Jersey, Oregon, and Virginia have already banned the sale of precise geolocation data. Matt Schwartz, a policy analyst at Consumer Reports who focuses on privacy, said opt-ins often contain verbiage allowing for the unlimited use, sharing, and sale of consumers' location and health data. Consumer Reports reported in September that when it had volunteers look at files companies had built about them, the information was often riddled with errors, and one person's report showed four different ages, listed him as both male and female, predicted three markedly different incomes, and listed his jobs as farmer, homemaker, and a self-employed white collar though he was none of those. Julien Cavanagh, a neurologist in Atlanta, said he now asks patients whether they are taking supplements bought online when they show up with unexplained neurological symptoms. Cavanagh said some of these sham treatments can be toxic, cause vitamin or micronutrient deficiencies, or counteract the action of their prescribed medications, and that the targeted ads are very common and insensitive.

In August, the Federal Trade Commission warned retailers about using private consumer data to increase prices. In May, the agency also placed limits on a data broker that the agency began investigating in 2022, and that settlement prohibits Idaho-based data broker Kochava and a subsidiary from selling, sharing or disclosing sensitive location data without consumer consent following allegations that the companies sold location data from hundreds of millions of mobile devices that could be used to trace the movements of people when they visited hospitals, churches, abortion clinics, and other sensitive locations. A 2024 report by Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis economists on the economic implications of digital advertising showed that the profit margins for three of the four biggest tech firms, Google parent Alphabet, Facebook parent Meta, and Microsoft, were at least twice as large as the services sector average. A 2019 study found that data brokers had data tied to more than 90% of Facebook accounts in the United States. A 2020 report by the Electronic Frontier Foundation said Google shared sensitive user data, including geolocation, device IDs, identifying cookies, and browsing history, with potentially hundreds of digital advertising companies.

The San Diego-based Privacy Rights Clearinghouse and the Electronic Frontier Foundation identified 750 data brokers operating in the U.S. as of last year. The Electronic Frontier Foundation said in an August policy paper that even when sensitive locations are stripped from a customer's profile, data brokers and advertisers can still track a person's route right up to the boundary of a sensitive zone and pick it up immediately upon departure, making it easy to infer the destination. Trujillo recommends people limit which apps track their location data and disable ad tracking on their phones, and it is also possible to turn off location data or put phones in airplane mode before heading to sensitive locations. At least 20 states allow their residents to demand that data brokers delete their personal data, but typically consumers must file requests with individual data brokers, and California has a centralized portal for requesting such opt-outs at privacy.ca.gov/drop/. Kochava did not respond to requests for comment, and neither Google nor Meta responded to requests for comment.

stories.Headline: EU Fines Tinder Owner €11 Million Over Data Privacy Violations
stories.Summary:
The European Union fined Match Group, the owner of the dating app Tinder, €11 million for failing to give users proper access to their personal data, AFP reported. Ireland's Data Protection Commission found that Tinder's "Download My Data" tool omitted certain categories of personal information. The tool also gave only summaries without clearly informing users, which violated EU data protection rules. The investigation was launched in 2020. The fine was announced on 13 November 2026.

The order requires Match Group to bring its data processing practices into compliance with the General Data Protection Regulation within three months. The GDPR is the EU's data protection rulebook. Ireland's Data Protection Commission carried out the investigation. The probe began in 2020 and ended with the €11 million penalty. The decision was reported by AFP and carried by BGNES on 13 November 2026.

Match Group rejected the findings of the Irish regulator. The company announced plans to appeal the decision. It insisted that Tinder maintains strong privacy protections for its users. The company did not accept the commission's conclusion about the data download tool. Match Group said it would challenge the penalty.

The fine affects Tinder users in the European Union who used the "Download My Data" tool. Ireland's Data Protection Commission is responsible for enforcing the GDPR against the company. The order gives Match Group three months to fix its practices. The case was investigated under EU data protection rules. Match Group's appeal means the penalty is not final.

The investigation into Tinder's data practices began in 2020. Ireland's Data Protection Commission examined the "Download My Data" tool during the probe. The regulator concluded that the tool fell short of GDPR requirements. The findings were reported by AFP on 13 November 2026. The BGNES article carried the AFP report the same day.

Match Group plans to appeal the €11 million fine. The order requires the company to comply with the GDPR within three months. The articles do not say when the appeal will be heard or decided. They do not say whether the fine will be suspended during the appeal. The articles leave open how Match Group will change the "Download My Data" tool.

stories.Headline: FAA launched new AI air traffic tool three days before national ground stop
stories.Summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop of all flights on November 13, 2026, only the third such stoppage in U.S. history. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed the ground stop at 4:16 p.m. ET. More than 2,000 flights were already affected, and flights into the U.S. were also halted. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told the press the stoppage was caused by a telecommunications outage, not a national security threat.

One day before the ground stop, ArsTechnica reported on the FAA's rollout of its new $875 million AI tool. The tool is the Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories system, known as SMART, a cloud-based platform designed to help controllers evaluate and manage national airspace. The FAA announced a rollout of SMART to 22 centers across the country on Nov. 10, three days before the ground stop. SMART had been active in Washington, DC airspace since at least Sept. 21, and according to the administration it had successfully helped reroute 180 flights. The FAA said SMART uses AI to analyze airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur.

Air Space Intelligence, the American aerospace and defense company behind SMART, built the system under an $875 million, 12-year contract. Mullin said of a possible SMART connection, "You can't rule out anything at this point," and said the process would find out what happened and appropriate actions would follow. He corrected a reporter's use of the term AI, saying the Trump administration officially calls the technology Super Intelligence, or SI, under a September executive order. He said the event was "just a telecommunications outage" while declining to exonerate the system deployed three days earlier. Air Space Intelligence posted a statement to X saying the ground stop was "not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC."

Former Transportation Department Inspector General Mary Schiavo said on CNN she did not know if SMART and the ground stop were linked, but called it "too much coincidence" that they were trying to start that moving that day. More than two dozen lawmakers wrote to Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford in October, relaying controller concerns that the frontline workforce had "little to no input" into SMART's development and received limited training and information during deployment. The letter said controllers raised the possibility SMART could interfere with decision-making by experienced controllers or hallucinate safety-critical information. Nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled, and people waited in Terminal B at Orlando International Airport on November 13. SMART is an advisory tool, not a control system, and sends routing recommendations to human controllers without flying or redirecting aircraft.

It centralizes 200 live data streams into one platform, and FAA specialists in Washington review recommendations before forwarding them to the Air Traffic Control System Command Center in Warrenton, Virginia, where local facility leadership at each of the 22 centers decides whether to accept or decline each suggestion. The FAA has said SMART cannot replace human controllers and cannot take over control of an aircraft. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year to modernize the U.S. air traffic control system, and Duffy has said another $30 billion will be required to complete the work. The 2023 NOTAM outage was traced to a single corrupted database file that propagated into the backup system.

As of the articles' writing, neither the FAA nor the Department of Homeland Security had established a cause for the ground stop. The failure involved the radio frequency systems pilots and controllers use to communicate, a layer of infrastructure the articles describe no further. Investigators had not ruled out that something in SMART's data pipeline failed. The articles leave open whether the deployment of SMART and the ground stop are connected.

stories.Headline: Microsoft apologises for global outage, blames network upgrade issue
stories.Summary:
Microsoft apologised for a global outage that disrupted Teams, Outlook, and Copilot AI for nearly 24 hours, according to TechGig on November 14, 2026. The company attributed the disruption to a technical failure during a network capacity upgrade, not a cyberattack. PC Gamer reported on November 13, 2026, that the outage began on November 12 and disrupted access to Microsoft 365 products for governments, hospitals, schools, and businesses around the world. Microsoft said neither AI nor malicious actors were at fault, but that the outage occurred as a result of an underlying infrastructural issue introduced during a network upgrade. The company ruled out a cyberattack as the cause, stating the disruption stemmed from a technical failure linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade.

Microsoft said the issue surfaced following a more recent network change, and that it had addressed the underlying issue and continued to restore service to remaining customers and regions. Given the scale of demand, Microsoft restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage, which took longer but helped ensure a stable restoration. Downdetector recorded over 130,000 reports of Outlook problems at the outage's peak, with disruptions reported across more than 70 countries. In India, the disruption affected customer-facing operations, particularly for airlines relying on Microsoft email services. IndiGo reported affected email support, Akasa Air noted delays in its email services, and Air India rerouted email services, ensuring flight operations remained unaffected.

Microsoft stated on X that it was deeply sorry for the disruption the incident had caused its customers and partners, adding that it knew the trust they place in its services and took that responsibility extremely seriously. The company said it was seeing broad recovery and stability across its services, and that this was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. Microsoft said the incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. It said it had addressed the underlying issue and continued to restore service to remaining customers and regions, and that given the scale of demand it restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. Microsoft said that while this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration, and that it would provide a full post-incident report once its review was complete.

PC Gamer noted that popular speculation had been eager to attribute the outage to vibe-coding, considering Microsoft's push for company-wide AI adoption, but the corporation said the outage was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents. PC Gamer said it was unclear whether another word was meant to follow cyber, and that it was just telling readers what the company wrote. PC Gamer also noted that Microsoft acknowledged the restoration of service was slower than many might have hoped, but said it brought services back online gradually to ensure stability. Financial services firms and other businesses in India also faced difficulties accessing research and handling client interactions, according to TechGig. TechGig reported that the widespread outage impacted several Microsoft services, preventing users from accessing essential tools for work, communication, and email.

PC Gamer reported that Microsoft laid off roughly 30,000 employees in the last four years, and said it was tempting to wonder whether any of the 10,000 employees Microsoft laid off in 2023 as part of its ongoing cost-cutting strategy might have known how to avoid the costly hiccup. PC Gamer also cited 6,000 employees laid off in May 2025, 9,000 laid off that July, and 4,800 laid off a year later, including 1,600 at Xbox with another 1,600 to follow. PC Gamer added that Microsoft extended voluntary buyout offers to 60,000 employees last month. TechGig reported that Microsoft emphasised there was no evidence pointing towards a deliberate attack.

Microsoft said it would provide a more detailed incident report once its internal review of the outage was complete, according to PC Gamer. Microsoft said it would provide a full post-incident report once its review was complete, according to its post on X. TechGig reported that recovery was executed gradually, validating stability at each stage to ensure a stable restoration. PC Gamer said it was unclear whether another word was meant to follow cyber in Microsoft's statement. TechGig reported that the company ruled out a cyberattack as the cause and that the issue surfaced following a more recent network change.

stories.Headline: IBM and Microsoft Launch AI Agent Platform
stories.Summary:
IBM and Microsoft announced a joint strategy called Imagine Enterprise on November 10, 2026. This new platform combines the cloud and AI technologies of Microsoft with IBM assets. IBM Consulting provides more than 6,000 AI agents and assets through IBM Consulting Advantage. The partnership creates industry specific agent frameworks for retail, insurance, and banking sectors. These companies aim to help enterprises automate various complex business and operational workflows.

The platform integrates Microsoft Copilot Studio for low code agent development across Microsoft 365. Microsoft offers capacity packs with 25,000 credits for ₹16,640 monthly in India. Microsoft Foundry provides the additional infrastructure needed for creating custom AI agents. The system targets automation for finance, HR, IT operations, customer service, and supply chain. It utilizes the combined resources of IBM Consulting and Microsoft cloud AI technologies.

IBM and Microsoft are responsible for the joint Imagine Enterprise strategy and platform. They stated that the partnership combines Microsoft cloud technology with thousands of IBM assets. IBM also made Agent Identity generally available in November 2026 for managing agents. The companies aim to solve problems where employees spend excessive time on repetitive tasks. They seek to reduce the time spent searching for information and updating applications.

Enterprise customers are affected by challenges like inaccurate AI decisions and unauthorized data access. Some users face failed task execution, which requires human intervention to complete transactions. Others struggle with disconnected business applications that cannot exchange information across different systems. CIOs are concerned about unpredictable operating costs from model tokens and API calls. There is also a need for audit trails to ensure better agent accountability.

The articles state that enterprise AI agent platforms are becoming a major technology investment. Companies like Salesforce, Google Cloud, AWS, ServiceNow, Oracle, and SAP offer competing platforms. Salesforce reported that Agentforce Coworker usage grew 21 fold over three months for users. Other platforms include OpenAI, Workday, Pegasystems, Palantir, Kore.ai, and Automation Anywhere for building autonomous agents. These tools address delays in customer service and IT support for many organizations.

Next, enterprises must evaluate agent permissions, integration complexity, and consumption based expenses for agents. Organizations will monitor response accuracy and CRM permissions to avoid exposing sensitive information. The articles leave open how companies will manage the risk of AI enabled breaches. It remains unclear how businesses will translate faster AI responses into lower operating costs. The long term impact on customer satisfaction from these autonomous agents is not specified.

stories.Headline: Nebius Stock Sinks as AI Cloud Provider Lowers Revenue Outlook, Lifts Capital Spending Guidance
stories.Summary:
Nebius Group, an AI cloud infrastructure provider listed on NASDAQ under NBIS, saw its shares drop 10% on Thursday, November 12, 2026, after it reported third-quarter results and issued a financial outlook that disappointed investors. The company reported revenue of $980.8 million for the quarter, a 571% year-over-year increase that exceeded the $907.5 million analyst consensus. Net loss narrowed to $37.5 million, or $0.13 per share, from $119.6 million, or $0.50 per share, in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted EBITDA reached $465.8 million, reversing an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.2 million a year earlier. Adjusted earnings were $0.30 per share, beating the adjusted loss of $0.61 per share expected in a separate analyst consensus.

Nebius forecast capital expenditures of $27 billion for 2026, above its previous guidance of $20 billion to $25 billion and above the $23.85 billion analyst estimate. For 2027, management guided capital expenditures of $40 billion to $45 billion, far above the $28.77 billion market consensus, or roughly 39% to 56% higher. The company expects 2026 revenue near the lower end of its prior $3 billion to $3.4 billion guidance, below the $3.35 billion analyst forecast, and introduced 2027 revenue guidance of $12 billion to $13 billion against a $12.09 billion consensus. Third-quarter spending on property, equipment and intangible assets reached $7.30 billion, compared with $955.5 million a year earlier. For the nine months ended September 30, revenue rose 549% to $1.96 billion from $302.1 million, and nine-month adjusted EBITDA was $831.5 million versus a $79.9 million loss.

Chief Executive Officer Arkady Volozh told shareholders that Nebius expects fiscal 2026 revenue near the lower end of its existing $3 billion to $3.4 billion forecast. The company said its 2027 guidance reflects planned expansion of its AI computing infrastructure, which requires considerable investment before new capacity can generate revenue. Management's 2027 outlook is broadly consistent with market expectations at the lower end but leaves significant uncertainty around infrastructure deployment and the timing of capacity additions. Nebius said the principal concern for investors is the relationship between its rapid revenue expansion and the capital required to deliver that growth. The company said infrastructure expansion remains central to achieving its $12 billion to $13 billion revenue target.

Before the earnings announcement, 15 of 22 analysts rated NBIS a Buy or higher, six recommended Hold and one rated it Sell, with an average price target of $278.05, about 80% above the November 11 closing price. Those targets preceded the latest outlook and may change following the report. Nebius shares had gained approximately 85% since the beginning of 2026 before the results, and rose 15.4% on November 11 to close at $154.69 as stronger earnings from AI infrastructure competitor CoreWeave supported sentiment across the neocloud sector. Nebius operates in the AI infrastructure market alongside CoreWeave and IREN, and its broader portfolio includes autonomous vehicle technology company Avride, education technology provider TripleTen and equity interests in ClickHouse and Toloka. Operating costs and expenses rose 237% to $930.4 million in the quarter, including depreciation and amortization of $354.7 million and selling, general and administrative expenses of $237.4 million.

For the first nine months, operating cash flow from continuing operations was positive at $4.23 billion, while net cash used in operating activities from continuing operations totaled $273 million in the third quarter. Total assets increased to $38.74 billion at September 30, compared with $12.43 billion at the end of 2025. The increase in capital spending places greater emphasis on Nebius' ability to deploy data center capacity, secure customer demand and convert infrastructure investments into future revenue. The company continued to report a GAAP net loss as depreciation, infrastructure costs and operating expenses increased. Nebius' stock performance will increasingly depend on whether revenue growth can justify an investment program potentially exceeding $40 billion annually.

A separate Yahoo Finance article on three AI stocks to watch, published Friday, November 13, 2026, highlighted Arista Networks, which sells data-driven networking hardware, EOS software and support connecting clients to cloud and AI data centers. Arista Networks reports about $11.9 billion in computer networks revenue and carries a market value near $248.5 billion. The article said accelerated adoption of AI and machine learning workloads continues to increase demand for high-bandwidth, low-latency networking infrastructure. Arista Networks is guiding AI fabrics revenue of at least $3.5 billion to $3.6 billion in 2026, with Etherlink already used by more than 1,000 customers. The article said the full growth screen surfaced 83 more companies not covered in the piece.

stories.Headline: Fed’s Barr says US should prepare for ‘serious’ AI job disruption, widening inequality
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr said on Thursday that the United States should be prepared for serious short-term disruptions in the job market because of artificial intelligence. He delivered the remarks at Yale University, in a speech prepared for delivery there. Barr did not predict such strains, but suggested that society should prepare for them as the technology spreads. He warned that, depending on how fast it is deployed, AI could begin displacing workers at scale and widen inequality in favor of investors. The articles report his remarks on November 13, 2026.

Barr pointed to labor's share of national income, which hit a record low of 52.8 percent in the second quarter of 2026. That share had held roughly steady between 60 percent and 65 percent from World War II until early this century. He said measurement issues explained some of the decline, but the downward trend remained after adjustments. Citing the Federal Reserve's latest Survey of Consumer Finances, he said the wealthiest 10 percent of households held nearly three-quarters of wealth, while the bottom half held about 2 percent. He said AI investment has raised gross domestic product, and that AI firms are pumping trillions of dollars into data centers and the computing resources they require.

Barr is a member of the Federal Reserve Board, whose chairman is Kevin Warsh. He said the distribution of AI's benefits would depend partly on competition, workers' bargaining power, and whether the technology replaces people or helps them become more productive. He said the implications remain uncertain, with much riding on whether competition among AI companies makes the technology a cheap and ubiquitous commodity, much like the internet became over time. In that case, he said, AI could democratize access to the skills and information that small businesses need to thrive. He urged that now is the time to begin considering how to address these challenges, while AI adoption is still at a relatively early stage.

Barr said no one knows the degree to which the benefits will be shared, and that signs are emerging of AI acting as a labor substitute in some sectors. Younger and less-experienced workers appear most exposed, he said, and he added that tasks with predictable outcomes and clear boundaries might be automated more quickly. Work involving judgement, relationships, coordination or creativity could instead benefit from technology that complements human skills. He said that if labor market changes happen quickly, it will be hard for workers to adjust, and dislocations might be large. Small businesses are also affected, since the outcome hinges on whether they can keep access to the technology to expand.

Barr said there has so far been relatively little displacement of workers by AI, and he noted evidence that the transition is enhancing the productivity of some workers. He said it is also increasing demand in some sectors and even creating new occupations. He said competition among AI companies has kept access relatively broad, and that some businesses might meet most of their needs with smaller language models rather than the most advanced systems. He said inequality has both widened and narrowed over the past century, shaped by technological change, education, taxation, regulation and workers' bargaining power. Some researchers believe AI has characteristics that have reinforced concentration of market power in past high-tech advances, he said, and the remarks built on his earlier speeches about AI and employment.

A public Fed forum is set for Monday in San Francisco, where a task force appointed by Warsh will explore what the technology may mean for the economy. Barr's comments followed midterm elections that swung partly on a backlash to the rapid AI buildout. Warsh has often mentioned the possibility of AI ushering in an era of rising productivity that could lower inflation. The timing of such gains is uncertain, however, and Barr said the main effect of deployment so far has been higher prices, with input pressure spilling over into areas like cellphones and gaming consoles. A number of his colleagues accept that AI investment is helping keep inflation above the Fed's target, which has firmed support for further interest rate increases, and the articles do not say how quickly any labor disruption might arrive.

stories.Headline: Anthropic expands Claude with workplace productivity tools
stories.Summary:
Anthropic expanded its Claude platform with new workplace productivity tools on Tuesday, November 12, 2026, to handle common office tasks. The company also released Claude Fable 5.2 on Monday, November 9, 2026, and the restricted Claude Mythos 5.2 for vetted organizations. These updates allow the AI to move beyond simple text generation and queries to compete with established productivity software suites. The new tools enable users to create spreadsheets, digital whiteboards, and data dashboards directly within the integrated Claude platform. This expansion positions the AI assistant against Microsoft 365 Copilot and Google Workspace Gemini in the professional productivity space.

Claude Sheets allows teams to edit formulas and organize data across multiple tabs, while Claude Whiteboards provides a shared digital space. Claude Data, previously called Dashboards, connects with Salesforce and Snowflake to generate visual data stories and narrated videos using certified definitions. The platform now includes interactive connectors for Adobe and Atlassian, plus plugins from Workday, NetSuite, and Salesforce for various business teams. Administrative controls let businesses manage employee access, set spending limits, and monitor usage through audit logs with encrypted enterprise data. Fable 5.2 costs 8 dollars per million input tokens and 40 dollars per million output tokens for its users.

Anthropic stated that Claude works around the user by knowing team work through connected tools and running within admin controls. The company claimed that Fable 5.2 generates output 30 percent faster than Fable 5.1 and blocks 55 percent fewer requests. They noted that the model can create customized tools like project status boards, account trackers, daily briefings, and contract review tables. Anthropic also mentioned that the new integrated approach allows users to carry context between different formats without repeating their instructions. The company highlighted that the platform now offers collaborative data organization, idea generation, and the creation of visual reports.

Jump Trading, Balyasny Asset Management, and XTX Markets use the model for quantitative research, while Box uses it for loan files. Box specifically uses the AI to flag mismatches between bank statement balances and salary deposits within the loan application files. Fable 5.2 scored 65 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Gemini 4 Carbon at 60 and Claude Opus 5.5. Other affected entities include cybersecurity and life sciences organizations that have access to the restricted sibling model known as Claude Mythos 5.2. These professional users can now utilize the AI for complex data analysis and collaborative workplace productivity within their own organizations.

The articles note that Anthropic previously launched Claude Opus 5.5, which costs 40 percent less to run than Opus 5. The company also updated its Usage Policy to protect models from humans and added a feature to send Gmail emails automatically. Anthropic recently took steps to block Claude from reverse engineering video games and implemented a text watermark that does not change responses. The Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index is an independent scorecard that both Anthropic and Google cite to compare their frontier AI models. These developments follow a trend of AI companies releasing specialized models for different tasks, such as planning and repetitive execution.

Anthropic is currently investigating an issue where some users are unable to authenticate their accounts on Claude.ai and the Claude Code tool. It remains unclear if these authentication problems are related to a massive outage that affected multiple Microsoft services on the same day. The articles leave open whether the authentication issues will be resolved quickly or if they indicate a larger systemic platform failure. Future updates are expected from the company status page as they continue to investigate the reports of login troubles on X. The long term impact of competing with Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace remains to be seen as the tools deploy.

stories.Headline: Databricks Launches New Always-on Genie: Autonomous AI for Complex Enterprise Work
stories.Summary:
Databricks announced the second generation of Genie on 11 November 2026, an always-on autonomous AI agent for enterprise work, according to SD Times. Databricks launched the update to expand its push to embed AI agents in existing corporate data and software environments, IT Brief Australia reported on 12 November 2026. The new version is designed to run continuously in the background and handle longer-running tasks without repeated user prompts. Workers can assign a goal, set boundaries, and let the system track progress, follow up on missing inputs, and return when a person needs to make a decision. The launch also includes Genie Search and new features in Genie Ontology, Databricks' framework for capturing business definitions, metrics, reporting lines, and processes.

Genie now operates in autonomous mode, running in the background using its own compute, and can manage daily personal tasks like email or Slack or bigger responsibilities like keeping a quarterly forecast on track. Key features include sub-agents that manage work in parallel, a priority inbox of items needing attention, and email alerts where each new alert arrives as its own unread email and updates go to the same thread. Genie Search lets teams index content in Google Drive, Jira, and Confluence without moving it, ingest it through Lakeflow Connect, or query applications live through MCP, and Databricks now offers more than 100 connectors. Genie Ontology adds support for business logic from external business intelligence tools and an organisational structure connector, and Ontology Manager is a new interface for teams to manage and govern business context. Genie is accessible through a web browser, mobile app, email, and ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, and Grok Bot, and agents can work across PDFs, contracts, and slide decks in Unity Catalog volumes without a separate vector index.

Ali Ghodsi, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Databricks, said Genie has made him a 10x more productive CEO and now doesn't wait for him to ask. He said Genie keeps up with his inbox every day, preps him for meetings, and runs in the background, coming back only when it needs a decision. He said it can do that because it knows how the company works, what revenue means, which numbers are official, and who can see what. He called that the power of horizontal context, and said Genie delivers it. Databricks said every action is grounded in Genie Ontology and stays within Unity Catalog permissions and Unity Gateway approval rules and budgets, and is fully auditable.

Jaime DeLanghe, Chief Product Officer of Slack, said teams make their best decisions when trusted context shows up in the flow of work, and that with Genie Agents connected to Slack, sales, finance, and operations teams can go from question to action without leaving the conversation. Marlissa Wong, Director of Data Engineering at Headspace, said AI is only as good as the definitions behind it, so Headspace built its Genie Agents on agreed, governed definitions, and now every answer matches. Wong said Headspace expanded self-service analytics by putting plain-language access to its data in the hands of teams across the business, not just analysts. Alan Khalil, Associate Director of Data Science and Engineering at HelloFresh, said that with Genie constantly analysing performance signals, HelloFresh improved programmatic ad ROI and reduced the time to identify ad winners on Meta by 75%. Khalil said Unity Gateway gives HelloFresh the flexibility to use the best model for each job without managing separate integrations.

Databricks is targeting a common point of tension in the adoption of AI agents by large organisations, IT Brief Australia reported. While many companies are experimenting with tools that can answer questions or complete tasks, concerns remain about giving those systems access to financial planning data, customer records, and internal documents. Under the new model, Genie can be used for operational work such as monitoring quarterly forecasts, tracking revenue trends, analysing employee survey responses, and identifying changes in customer usage patterns. SD Times reported that much of what it takes to do complex projects well lives across multiple platforms and even in people's heads, such as which accounts need attention, what triggers an escalation, and who approves a change. SD Times reported that an enterprise assistant can only take that on if it knows the business, can reach the systems teams already use, and follows correct permissions and access controls.

Databricks said Genie and Genie Ontology are generally available, while Genie Search, Ontology Manager, and the always-on version of Genie are being rolled out through preview and beta programmes. SD Times reported that new MCP connectors such as Atlassian, Google Drive and GitHub, along with OpenSharing for Genie Agents, allow teams to collaborate with partners without exposing underlying data. SD Times reported that Genie MCP lets AI tools and agents use Genie Ontology and Genie Search to find and access enterprise knowledge. IT Brief Australia reported that Genie can delegate work to sub-agents, present outstanding issues in a priority inbox, and send email alerts when user input is required. Databricks said Genie can generate dynamic, data-driven slides, dashboards, and interactive reports that are grounded in governed data and stay current as that data changes.

stories.Headline: What Does CoreWeave (CRWV) Winning A New AI Training Deal Mean?
stories.Summary:
CoreWeave shares jumped 10 per cent on Wednesday, setting off a rally in battered AI cloud stocks, after the company reported strong revenue growth from its heavy spending. The company also signaled a pullback from the borrowing binge that had raised alarms about an AI bubble. The earnings lifted shares of key CoreWeave backer Nvidia by 5 per cent, following a bruising two-day slide. That slide was driven by worries about CEO Jensen Huang's future at the company after his affair with a Chinese businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing. Shares of so-called neoclouds including Nebius and Iren also rallied, after weeks of turmoil over fears that debt-fueled data center expansion could backfire if AI demand slows.

CoreWeave raised its annual revenue forecast and said it would not tap unsecured debt markets, following a recent spike in borrowing costs. The company said cash flow from existing contracts would cover both current and future debt repayments. In premarket trading, Nebius, Iren, Oracle and Applied Digital climbed between 4.7 per cent and 11.8 per cent. All of those stocks except Nebius had lost 32 per cent to 48 per cent this year as of Tuesday, while Nebius had surged 60 per cent. Together, the cloud companies including CoreWeave were set to gain more than $25 billion in market value on the day, while Nvidia alone stood to add about $210 billion if the gains hold.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told Reuters on Tuesday that greater scrutiny could slow data center construction across the industry. He did not expect it to significantly alter the company's expansion plans or drive up its costs. The company itself said it would avoid unsecured debt markets and rely on cash flow from existing contracts to meet its debt repayments. Intrator's comments came after last week's Democratic midterm sweep, which dealt another blow to the AI industry. The company's raised annual revenue forecast was central to the results that investors cheered on Wednesday.

Bernstein analysts led by Madison Rezaei said CoreWeave delivered about the best quarter they could have asked for. In a client note, they said the stats were good-to-great, funding concerns were addressed and the strategic moves make sense. The analysts also warned that CoreWeave will be among the first and hardest hit when the crunch in AI computing capacity eases. Several winning candidates in the Democratic midterm sweep campaigned for tighter regulation and for moratoriums on new data center construction, including in the crucial market of Texas. Investors in AI infrastructure stocks, including the neoclouds and Nvidia, had reason to cheer after the results.

The articles describe how the neocloud stocks had faced weeks of turmoil on fears that their debt-fueled data center expansion could backfire if AI demand slows. CoreWeave's results came after a recent spike in borrowing costs that prompted the company to rule out unsecured debt markets. The risks of mistiming AI investments became evident on Tuesday, when SoftBank took a $3.7 billion writedown on non-refundable payments for equipment to power its US data centers. That writedown pushed the Japanese tech investor to a second-quarter net loss of $7 billion, its first in nearly two years. Nvidia had suffered a two-day slide over worries about Huang's future, tied to his affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a spy for Beijing.

Nebius is due to report results before Thursday's opening bell, giving investors the next look at the neocloud group. The articles do not say whether the rally across AI cloud stocks will hold, noting only that the market value gains are set if they do. They also leave open how far scrutiny and proposed data center moratoriums, including in Texas, will slow construction across the industry. It remains unclear how Huang's situation will play out at Nvidia, since the articles describe only the worries that drove its two-day slide. The articles give no date for when the crunch in AI computing capacity might ease, which Bernstein says would hit CoreWeave first and hardest.

stories.Headline: BIM Trichy and UT Arlington Redefine International Education: US Master's Degree in AI for Business Comes to India
stories.Summary:
Bharathidasan Institute of Management, a business school based in Tiruchirappalli, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with The University of Texas at Arlington. The agreement covers a joint Master of Science in Artificial Intelligence for Business, known by the abbreviation MSAIB. The signing was reported by The Hindu BusinessLine on November 13, 2026, and a photograph shows officials from both institutions at the ceremony. The programme is aimed at working professionals and will integrate AI machine learning, data engineering and generative AI into business strategy. It will be hosted at IIT Madras Research Park rather than at either partner's own campus.

The programme will begin with an initial trial cohort of 25 students, and faculty from the University of Texas at Arlington will facilitate it. It carries an indicative tuition fee of US$27,000, set as an alternative to the substantially higher overall cost of two years of full-time residential study in the United States. The hybrid learning model uses eight-week courses, with seven weeks of online instruction followed by one week of in-person learning. Students will be taught by the American university's faculty throughout the programme. They will also take part in a one-week immersion in the United States, which includes company visits, interactions with business executives and exposure to industry applications of artificial intelligence.

Ravi Appasamy, Chairman of the Board of Governors at BIM Tiruchirappalli, described the partnership as a deliberate step in building a globally recognised institution. He said the Board is firmly committed to positioning BIM as globally connected, academically distinguished and industry-relevant. He added that BIM is entering a new phase of its transformational journey, and that the institute is not simply building for the next decade. In his words, it is laying the foundations for the next generation of management education. Asit K. Barma, Director of BIM Tiruchirappalli, was also at the signing, as was Fernando Jaramillo, Associate Dean of Academic Affairs at the Texas university.

Radha K. Mahapatra, Chair and Professor of Information Systems and Operations Management at the University of Texas at Arlington, spoke about how students will be admitted. He said enrolments will be conducted through the university's own specialised framework. Although the programme is designed for working professionals, he said the university is also open to selecting capable students who have just completed their undergraduate studies. Separately, Anurag Behar, CEO of the Azim Premji Foundation, wrote in Mint on November 11, 2026 that India's higher education is in worse shape than its school education. He argued that artificial intelligence could be the death blow to the country's higher education institutions if the existing mess is perpetuated.

The partnership comes at a time when international student mobility has been disrupted by visa policies, rising education and living costs, and geopolitical developments. The Institute of International Education's Open Doors 2025 report said new international student enrolments in the US fell by 7 per cent. Australia saw international student commencements drop by 12 per cent compared with the corresponding period. The UK reported a 16 per cent year-over-year decline in sponsored study visa grants to Indian nationals. Meanwhile, several global universities have set up in India, including the University of Liverpool in Bengaluru, the University of Bristol in Mumbai and the University of Western Australia in Mumbai and Chennai.

Behar's article offers its own account of the problems facing Indian higher education. He argues that many college classrooms sit empty because neither students nor teachers show up, and that research is conflated with teaching. He says public funding has been squeezed while enrolment ambitions have grown, and that his estimate is only 10 to 15 per cent of institutions are serious about their work. He pictures a loop in which a machine prepares the lesson, another writes the student's answer and a third marks it, so that no human mind learns anything. He calls for AI to be mostly banished from education and for a good higher education system to be built on new foundations.

The articles say the programme will start with a trial cohort of 25 students, but they give no start date for classes or for the first intake. They do not say how many students might be admitted after the trial cohort, or how the programme will be assessed. The articles do not say whether the Master's degree will be awarded by the University of Texas at Arlington, by BIM or jointly by both. They also leave open when applications will open and what admission criteria the university's own framework will use. The sources do not explain how the indicative tuition fee of US$27,000 might change, or whether any part of the cost will be covered by the partners.

stories.Headline: Democratic political group launches new push to shape AI agenda before 2028
stories.Summary:
A Democratic political organization called Tomorrow Together launched a new effort to shape the artificial intelligence agenda before the 2028 presidential campaign. This initiative was announced on November 12, 2026, during a two day event called the What's Next conference held in Denver. The group wants to change how the party talks with voters about the risks and regulations of this powerful technology. They aim to create a stark contrast with President Donald Trump, who opposes the regulation of artificial intelligence. The organization is deepening its investment in this issue to prepare for future political battles and potential technology incidents.

The new research initiative requires an initial investment of 1.1 million dollars to start its work on the AI agenda. Tomorrow Together previously spent 6.5 million dollars on behalf of candidates who called for more regulation of data centers. These efforts took place during the midterms to counter the huge campaign war chest belonging to the technology industry. The group pushed for new limits on artificial intelligence and data centers to protect humans from emerging technological risks. This push follows warnings that AI may soon enter a phase where it can build new versions of itself.

Maddie Kriger, the chief program officer, said getting this right is critical to winning votes from the American people. She stated that the group wants to be prepared to take action if worse AI incidents occur next year. Co-founder Karthik Ganapathy said he would rather be on the Democratic side than the Republican side on this issue. Co-founder Rob Flaherty argued that Democrats now have the lead because voters want to see technology being regulated. They believe the party can become the primary force pushing for necessary guardrails on the development of artificial intelligence.

Data analyst David Shor told the Denver crowd that they are watching the birth of a new political issue. He described artificial intelligence as a rare topic where voters from both political parties embrace the idea of regulation. The effort affects voters who are concerned about the risks that AI poses to humans during this new phase. Some Republicans are affected, including Florida Governor Ron DeSantis, who has distanced himself from the pro industry stance of Trump. The group believes Trump has embraced a wildly unpopular position by opposing the regulation of this powerful new technology.

The articles state that Democrats are meeting in Denver to celebrate their sweeping wins in the recent midterm races. This gathering serves as an opportunity for party leaders to chart a course toward the next presidential campaign cycle. The background includes a political environment where the industry has used a huge war chest to influence the midterms. There are fresh warnings that AI development is moving toward a stage where the technology can self replicate. This context has led the organization to view AI as a key point of contrast against the current president.

The group will now work to shape the party's messaging to better address the concerns of voters before 2028. They will monitor the situation to see if more AI incidents occur over the next year as development continues. The articles leave open whether other Republicans will follow Governor Ron DeSantis in distancing themselves from the president's views. It remains unclear how the technology industry will respond to the increased Democratic push for stricter regulatory guardrails. The final impact of the 1.1 million dollar research initiative on the 2028 election is not yet known.

It described them as the co-founders behind the AI startup's rise.

The Economic Times, in a report dated November 11, 2026, placed Surya Midha among the five youngest billionaires who built their fortunes on artificial intelligence. That article also named Fabian Hedin and Nvidia among its tags on the subject. It did not give a separate net worth figure for Midha beyond the India Weekly numbers. The India Weekly report tied the doubled fortunes directly to Mercor hitting the $20 billion mark. Both articles frame the wealth as coming from the AI boom.

The articles attribute the wealth to Hiremath and Midha as the two co-founders of Mercor. India Weekly states their worth as $4.2 billion each at the $20 billion valuation. The Economic Times lists Midha among the youngest billionaires in AI, alongside the other names in its set. Neither article quotes either founder directly in the text provided. The context given is the broader AI boom, which both articles cite as the force behind these fortunes. India Weekly ties the doubling to the startup's jump to a $20 billion valuation. The Economic Times frames the pair within a wider group of young billionaires made by artificial intelligence. Neither article says what happens next for Mercor or the two founders. stories.Headline: IIT Jammu, NTT DATA to set up AI Centre of Excellence
stories.Summary:
The Indian Institute of Technology Jammu and NTT DATA announced a strategic collaboration to establish an Artificial Intelligence Centre of Excellence at IIT Jammu. NTT DATA is described as a global leader in digital business and technology services. The announcement was reported by Daily Excelsior on 13 November 2026 from Jammu. NTT DATA announced the collaboration in a statement on 13 November 2026, according to Elets Technomedia. The two organisations announced the partnership to develop AI for flood warnings and regional languages.

The proposed Centre will focus on using Artificial Intelligence and emerging technologies to address regional challenges and strengthen climate and disaster resilience. It will also develop technology talent and create new opportunities for innovation and entrepreneurship in Jammu and Kashmir. The collaboration will bring together IIT Jammu's academic and research capabilities with NTT DATA's global technology expertise and industry experience. NTT DATA will leverage its global network of Innovation Centres to connect IIT Jammu's research capabilities with industry requirements and advanced technology expertise. The Centre of Excellence will organise its activities around four principal areas: secure and responsible AI, digital twins, physical AI, and a laboratory dedicated to research commercialisation and startup development.

Prof. Manoj Gaur, Director of IIT Jammu, said the collaboration aims to create an environment where ideas can move from research to real-world application. He said it will provide students, researchers and faculty with opportunities to address challenges particularly relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. He said it will also strengthen efforts towards research commercialisation, technology entrepreneurship and the development of a strong deep-tech ecosystem in the region. Avinash Joshi, Executive Managing Director for India at NTT DATA, said the collaboration would combine the company's international technology expertise with local knowledge to develop solutions relevant to Jammu and Kashmir. Joshi said the partnership would give researchers and students a pathway to turn promising ideas into practical solutions and commercial applications.

The proposed AI-CoE will provide opportunities for students, researchers and faculty to work with industry on real-world challenges and develop technology solutions with potential applications across Jammu & Kashmir and beyond. Jammu & Kashmir's mountainous terrain and river systems present complex challenges related to floods, landslides, infrastructure planning and emergency response. Potential applications include flood monitoring and early-warning systems for the Tawi and Chenab river basins, along with technology-based approaches for monitoring landslide and flood risks. The proposed AI-CoE will explore secure and responsible AI, digital twins and physical AI, combining AI with robotics, computer vision, IoT and edge technologies for applications in infrastructure monitoring, environmental monitoring, autonomous systems and public safety. The partnership will also support research into Indian languages, including Dogri, while helping students and researchers develop technologies that could eventually be commercialised or used by public institutions.

The partnership builds on India's wider efforts to incorporate advanced computing into flood forecasting. In July 2025, the Ministry of Jal Shakti inaugurated C-FLOOD, a digital platform developed through collaboration between the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, the Central Water Commission and the National Remote Sensing Centre. The platform provides flood inundation forecasts up to two days in advance, including village-level maps and predicted water levels. The Central Water Commission has also been developing AI and machine learning models to improve short-range flood forecasting across its monitoring network. The centre is the latest in a run of industry-backed AI labs at Indian institutes, after IIT Delhi's ₹9 crore AI research pact with Walmart Global Tech earlier this month.

The physical AI track places IIT Jammu alongside institutes such as IIT Kharagpur, which is building India's first dedicated School of Physical AI. The partnership announcement does not confirm the launch of a specific Dogri-language AI model or application. The partners have not disclosed the total investment, project implementation schedule or expected dates for deploying the proposed technologies. Residents in flood-prone areas should continue relying on official weather and disaster management advisories until any new AI-based warning systems are formally validated and introduced. The effectiveness of such systems would depend on the quality of available data, the accuracy of predictions and their integration with existing disaster management mechanisms.

stories.Headline: DEEPX Begins Mask Production for Samsung 2nm AI Chip, Targets Q4 2027 Mass Production
stories.Summary:
The fabless semiconductor company DEEPX announced on November 10 that it finished the design of its DX-M2 artificial intelligence chip. The company completed the mask tape-out for prototype production in early November. This process involves transferring finalized design data to the foundry and correcting lithography distortions. Photomask production will now follow this milestone.

The project requires an investment of over $100 million for production engineering and performance verification. The chip uses Samsung Electronics' SF2P second-generation 2-nanometer foundry process. DEEPX expects to receive its first silicon chips in March 2027 and provide customer samples in the second quarter. Initial mass production is scheduled for the fourth quarter of 2027, with global expansion starting in 2028.

DEEPX is responsible for the project and stated that the chip targets industrial systems, robotics, and AI personal computers. The company noted the DX-M2 runs generative AI workloads, such as vision-language and large language models, using about 5 watts. This design allows AI to run directly on devices instead of remote data centers. Such an approach reduces costs, energy use, and data delays.

This effort follows the August 2025 mass production of the DX-M1 chip, which used a 5nm process. By October 2026, DEEPX had secured 88 purchase orders worth roughly $13.3 million across 10 countries. The company now forecasts 2026 revenue of $40 million, which is more than double its previous target. The DX-M2 also earned a CES 2027 Innovation Award in the AI category.
