stories.Headline: MIT Researchers Create Roadmap to Help Organizations Mitigate AI Risks
stories.Summary:
Researchers at MIT created a roadmap to help organizations mitigate risks from artificial intelligence. This project was announced on November 13, 2026, in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The team developed a free public database called the AI Risk Mitigation Repository. It catalogs 2,206 proposed safeguards drawn from 47 existing governance and risk-management frameworks. This resource helps organizations identify practical ways to manage risks and find important gaps.

The repository organizes each safeguard by the risk it addresses and the responsible actor. It also tracks when action should occur during the AI lifecycle and how it reduces risk. The project involved MIT FutureTech, the MIT Sloan School of Management, and the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. Collaborators included the University of Queensland, IBM Research, Stanford University, the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, and the United Nations University. The team also created a reporting framework called PRIMER for consistent and transparent descriptions.

Neil Thompson is the director of MIT FutureTech and a principal research scientist. He stated that organizations recognize the need to address AI risks but lack practical action steps. He noted that a common way to organize safeguards is necessary to coordinate efforts and evaluate options. Peter Slattery is a research scientist at MIT FutureTech and a contributor to the study. He said the resource helps decision-makers understand existing options and where critical gaps remain.

The study found that 55 percent of mitigations focus on AI systems, while others target organizational processes. Developers are responsible for 41 percent of safeguards, and deploying organizations account for 33 percent. Governance actors, including regulators and policymakers, are responsible for another significant share of the proposed interventions. Companies can use the repository to support internal risk-management efforts for their specific AI systems. Policymakers can explore different regulatory approaches, and researchers can investigate which safeguards are actually effective.

The AI Risk Mitigation Repository is part of the MIT AI Risk Initiative led through MIT FutureTech. This initiative previously launched the AI Risk Repository, which focused on cataloging potential AI risks. The current project shifts the focus toward identifying and organizing solutions to those risks. The repository covers technical improvements, organizational policies, industry standards, audits, transparency measures, public oversight, and international coordination. It includes an interactive explorer to search safeguards by category and relate them to different risks.

The researchers found that organizational accountability and responsibility was the largest category at 13.4 percent. However, human oversight of autonomous agents and society's resilience from disruptions each accounted for less than 2 percent. Stewardship of computing resources for advanced AI systems also represented less than 2 percent of documented mitigations. These underrepresented areas are identified as important opportunities for future work as AI systems become more capable. The articles leave open which specific mitigations will prove most effective in practice over time.

Articles.Title: MIT Researchers Create Roadmap to Help Organizations Mitigate AI Risks

stories.Headline: Shield AI Opens Bengaluru Engineering Office to Build Defence Autonomy Software
stories.Summary:
Shield AI, a US defence technology company, opened an engineering office in Bengaluru on 13 November 2026 to develop and test autonomy software for Indian aircraft and defence systems. The office is located at GoodWorks GCC Nexus in Bengaluru and is the company's second in India, after its New Delhi office opened in April 2026. The Bengaluru team will focus on Hivemind, the company's software platform for developing, deploying and operating autonomous systems. The company said it will hire engineers specialising in autonomy, flight software, simulation, systems integration, and testing and evaluation. The Bengaluru team will work with the Delhi office, which leads engagement with the Ministry of Defence, the Indian armed forces and Indian industry.

In November 2024, Shield AI partnered with JSW Defence to indigenise and manufacture its V-BAT unmanned aircraft system in India, and JSW Group committed $90 million to the project. JSW Defence began construction of the V-BAT facility in December 2025 at EMC Maheshwaram in Hyderabad. In January 2026, Shield AI said it had been selected to supply V-BAT aircraft and licences for its Hivemind autonomy software to the Indian Army. According to the company, Hivemind has been piloted across more than 40 platforms, including F-16 fighter aircraft, jet-powered uncrewed aircraft, helicopters, uncrewed surface vessels, ground vehicles and a satellite in low Earth orbit. Karnataka IT Secretary Dr Manjula N. welcomed the expansion, saying the Bengaluru engineering centre would create opportunities for specialised talent and strengthen the state's capabilities in emerging technologies.

Sarjan Shah, Managing Director for India at Shield AI, said New Delhi brought the company closer to its customers while Bengaluru gives it the engineering team to build for them. He said self-reliance in defence depends on the software layer, and that the company is hiring in Bengaluru to build, test and improve mission autonomy for Indian platforms so the armed forces can own the capability for the long term. The announcement comes as India pushes for greater domestic development of defence technologies. In October 2026, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh released the Indian Army's Land Warfare Doctrine 2026 and called for faster progress in artificial intelligence and autonomous systems.

Articles.Title: Shield AI Opens Bengaluru Engineering Office to Build Defence Autonomy Software - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: The great Generative AI unraveling
stories.Summary:
On November 13, 2026, the US stock market fell sharply, with about $1 trillion wiped out in 40 minutes, according to a post by The Macro Paper cited by Gary Marcus. Marcus wrote that Nvidia was down 29% over six months, Oracle 35%, CoreWeave 54%, and Anthropic's perceived valuation 25% in weeks. He said Anthropic had hoped for a $2 trillion valuation at IPO and would now count itself lucky to get $1.5 trillion. He also said a neocloud company called N-Scale was in serious trouble after overcommitting, and that the news broke during his appearance on CNBC's Fast Money with host Melissa Lee.

Marcus said generative AI companies followed the same path with similar techniques and datasets, so OpenAI could not keep its lead, nobody had much of a technical moat, and price wars would make profits hard. He said training is very expensive and getting more so, citing a reported $10 billion cost to develop the Claude 5.5 model family, and that inference is expensive too. He said studies show a lack of return on investment and that the systems remain poor at following instructions. He also pointed to the Klarna effect, in which companies rehire humans after making extravagant claims about AI.

Marcus said Nvidia's interim CEO, Colette Kress, may be less inclined than Jensen to make big bets, and might refuse to prop up Nscale. He said that if Nvidia stops acting like everybody's banker, a bunch of neocloud companies are in trouble and Anthropic's IPO could be jeopardized. He cited a Bloomberg post by Jesse Felder saying banks are dumping AI loans, tech bond buyers are saying no more, and hedge funds are selling. Marcus said OpenAI, Anthropic, Nscale and CoreWeave have never been demonstrably profitable, apart from one quarter when Anthropic received heavy subsidies from Musk, and that they may now have to stand on their own.

Marcus said he had warned since August 2023 that generative AI might be a financial dud, and that hypey valuations lasted longer than he expected. He said the change in regime at Nvidia may have massive repercussions because so much rested on Jensen making big bets on companies Nvidia was effectively subsidizing. He said his sense, which could be wrong, is that the market has finally picked up on the irrationality of generative AI's economics. He said we may soon see a lot more moments like the N-Scale one.

Articles.Title: The great Generative AI unraveling

stories.Headline: Can Karnataka’s AI Hub Ease Compute Costs for Women-Led Startups?
stories.Summary:
Women founders raised concerns about access to computing at the Women Entrepreneurs’ Mixer, an event organised by Karnataka’s Department of Electronics, IT and Biotechnology ahead of the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit. Priyanka Gangishetty, co-founder of Vuha AI, which builds industrial and AI smart cameras, asked whether the government could provide subsidised GPUs, hardware or facilities where startups could train their models. She said anyone in the AI space needs a lot of compute GPUs and asked whether startups could get them at a more subsidised rate than what was available. Government officials said they would examine proposals for subsidised computing and shared facilities.

Prof Debabrata Das, associated with the proposed ₹35 crore AI Hub at IIIT-Bangalore, said hardware costs had risen roughly four times in the past year, especially for memory and GPUs. He said the IndiaAI Mission provides computing through its own channel, not through the state government, and that Karnataka already gives capital expenditure support to hardware companies through its electronics system design and manufacturing and startup schemes. He said the AI Hub is planning an AI Living Lab where startups could book slots to access computing resources and test their solutions. He cautioned that computing capacity and memory availability were global constraints and could remain so for another year and a half.

Dr Manjula N, IAS Secretary of Electronics, ITBT and S&T in the Karnataka government, asked Das to examine whether the state could provide further compute subsidies through the proposed facility. She said the state was preparing a policy to make government data available to companies based on their requirements. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta, CEO of KDEM, said the organisation could help connect women-led startups with manufacturing companies, global capability centres and large enterprises, and he highlighted the Government First initiative, which provides pilot support of up to ₹25 lakh. Under ELEVATE Shakti 2026, 63 women-led startups were selected with grant support of ₹23.19 crore committed, and the broader ELEVATE Grant-in-Aid Programme has supported more than 400 women-led startups since 2017 with committed assistance of ₹118.98 crore.

The IndiaAI Mission has secured and allotted 62,000 GPUs to date, but their utilisation remains marginal. According to KDEM, Karnataka accounts for roughly 10% of India’s electronic output and 64% of ESDM exports. Dr Manjula said the government had identified 11 technology business incubators outside Bengaluru and that the state is setting up 50 AI learning labs in government colleges across tier-2 and tier-3 cities. KDEM has also been organising technology events that bring industry leaders to cities outside Bengaluru, such as Mysuru, Mangaluru and the Belagavi-Hubballi Cluster.

Articles.Title: Can Karnataka’s AI Hub Ease Compute Costs for Women-Led Startups? - Analytics India Magazine

stories.Headline: When AI agents become enterprise users, the infrastructure equation changes - ET CIO
stories.Summary:
On November 13, 2026, ETCIO published a report on an ETCIO, Redis executive roundtable held in Bengaluru, where Redis CEO Rowan Trollope joined senior AI and technology leaders to discuss agentic AI in the enterprise. The discussion focused on how AI agents are becoming users of enterprise systems in their own right. A single employee could start hundreds of autonomous processes, each retrieving information, querying databases, calling tools, or triggering further actions. Multiplied across a company, this activity changes infrastructure needs for capacity, concurrency, and performance.

The article says enterprises are moving AI applications faster than their data architectures, context management, and operational infrastructure. It describes a context gap, where knowledge sits in disconnected systems and in employees' experience, emails, and undocumented processes. Trollope said even a simple customer revenue query could return conflicting answers from different systems, which led Redis to reorganize its information architecture and use agents to structure institutional knowledge into an ontology. Trollope raised the possibility of an enterprise with 10,000 employees eventually supporting millions of agentic processes, and he identified context engineering as a critical discipline, covering the selection of relevant data, tools, and memory plus systematic evaluation of agent performance.

The article gives examples of operational use. In connected city infrastructure, agentic capabilities support configurable street-light maintenance workflows. In customer support spanning over 100 systems, AI-enabled workflows have shown potential to cut resolution cycles from weeks or months to about five minutes. The article argues that differentiation will come less from foundation models, which are widely accessible, and more from proprietary knowledge, domain expertise, context, memory, recommendation capabilities, and customer distribution, along with the economics of retrieval, persistent memory, storage, repeated tool calls, and backend interactions.

The article frames the shift as a question of enterprise readiness, since model intelligence alone cannot make up for fragmented knowledge, inconsistent data definitions, or infrastructure that cannot sustain machine-driven workloads. It says the next phase will require an integrated view of context, architecture, economics, and business outcomes. The priority, it says, is not maximizing the number of autonomous agents but making sure they can access reliable information, operate within enterprise controls, and deliver measurable improvements. The article is part of ETCIO's Brand Connect Initiative and ends with a call to connect with Redis.

Articles.Title: When AI agents become enterprise users, the infrastructure equation changes - ET CIO

stories.Headline: Coursera launches AI series for role-based workplace skills
stories.Summary:
Coursera launched a set of 12 learning plans called AI Series, the company announced on 12 November 2026. The plans focus on artificial intelligence skills for specific professions, covering roles in business, finance, healthcare, data, cybersecurity, software development and engineering. Each series combines courses, specialisations and hands-on projects from universities, companies and subject specialists. The plans are organised around skills maps that draw on industry research, professional standards and labour-market data.

The first group of plans covers business leadership, project management, finance and accounting, product management, digital marketing, and healthcare management and operations. A second group covers data analytics, cybersecurity, information technology, software development, and two engineering tracks, AI Engineering: Using Coding Agents Series and AI Engineering: Building and Deploying AI Applications Series. Coursera said the engineering tracks are based on the AI Engineering Skills Map created by Andrew Ng and informed by more than 10,000 job postings and interviews with practitioners. Content comes from providers including Saïd Business School at the University of Oxford, Vanderbilt University, Duke University, Stanford Online, the University of Glasgow, Google Cloud, Microsoft, IBM, Adobe, Meta, AWS, Anthropic, UiPath and DeepLearning.AI.

Coursera linked the launch to its 2025 Learner Outcomes Report on the workplace effects of generative AI training. According to the company, 94% of surveyed full-time professionals who completed GenAI content reported a positive impact at work, and 42% said they had received a salary increase since enrolling. Dr Jules White, Senior Advisor to the Chancellor on Generative AI at Vanderbilt University, said professionals need structured, expert-led learning to master the patterns of solving problems with AI, comparing it to how people are taught to read and write. Several series focus on using AI in existing tasks rather than retraining for new occupations, such as forecasting and reporting in finance and threat detection in cybersecurity.

The launch is aimed at professionals seeking more structured routes into AI as the technology spreads across workplaces. The series is designed to help learners apply AI in practical settings, including prompting, workflow design and application building. Coursera said the figures point to a growing market for short-form, role-based technical education as employers test how AI is changing work. They also reflect a shift in online learning towards narrower, job-linked pathways rather than broad subject catalogues.

Articles.Title: Coursera launches AI series for role-based workplace skills - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: IRS eyes agentic AI tool to help staffers process potential fraud cases
stories.Summary:
The IRS is piloting an agentic AI tool to help staff process potential fraud cases, as announced on Friday, November 13, 2026. Jim Clifford, the director of return integrity and compliance services in the Taxpayer Service Division, shared these plans during a panel at the ACT-IAC Service Delivery and Experience Summit. The agency already uses machine-learning models to flag anomalies in tax returns. This new tool will focus on the back end of the process to make employees more efficient.

The technology will handle clerical and rote tasks, such as organizing taxpayer correspondence and reading submitted documents. Specifically, the AI will review responses, summarize information, and build a case before handing it to a human. This change aims to reduce the constraints on how fast workers can operate, though humans will still make all final judgments. While there is no official deployment timeline, the pilot will eventually scale to other IRS areas if it is successful.

Jim Clifford stated that the agency is already very accurate at stopping identity theft refund fraud, but the overall cost of fraud remains too high. He noted that fraudsters make about 1 billion attempts every month to steal taxpayer information. According to the Government Accountability Office, the federal government loses between $116 billion and $304 billion annually to tax fraud. Clifford believes the agency is generally good at protecting data, despite a few instances of inappropriate releases.

The IRS is also looking for more interoperability and data-sharing with state, local, and other federal governments. Clifford mentioned that current legislative and regulatory constraints limit this sharing, but APIs and AI could allow for safe information exchange. He believes these breakthroughs would better protect and serve American taxpayers. The agency will continue testing the agentic AI tool as part of a separate workstream.

Articles.Title: IRS eyes agentic AI tool to help staffers process potential fraud cases

stories.Headline: NiCE's next-generation Cognigy bets the hard part of AI agents is running them, not building them
stories.Summary:
NiCE Ltd. launched the next generation of NiCE Cognigy this week, SiliconANGLE reported on November 13, 2026. The release includes a redesigned Agentic Experience Studio and an AI Assist companion spanning the building, testing and improvement of agents. It adds reusable “skills” that package instructions and tools, turn-by-turn tracing and native voice-to-voice model support. Default speech-to-text, text-to-speech and large language models are now included in the per-conversation price. Premium models from Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Anthropic are available with a few clicks and billed by usage.

Nhu Ho, senior product marketing manager at NiCE Cognigy, opened an analyst briefing with a chart showing AI worked on its own for seconds in 2020, minutes in 2024 and roughly 16 hours this year. The footnote calculated that figure at a 50% success rate. Clement Boutier, director of product management, said the large number of options when configuring an agent creates friction to get started, which slows things down. The new studio lets a builder stand up an agent in a few clicks, with models already provisioned, while full access to the agent’s system prompt sits in advanced sections. Boutier described three builder personas: smaller businesses building simple agents, contact center administrators and team leads, and engineers at technically sophisticated companies.

Ho said capable and dependable do not always mean the same thing, and that is exactly where the platform matters. Boutier said hybrid “is actually where most of our customers are,” while fully agentic deployments are at the beginning of the adoption curve. Ho described the release as “an evolution, not a replacement,” with production deployments, application programming interfaces and integrations continuing to run unchanged. Boutier said you can have the best builder experience, but without a feedback loop on what you are building you will never build a great agent. Boutier said responsibility is shared: “We offer the tools and the platform, but we cannot 100% control what they put in it.”

The Simulator now supports multivariate testing of up to 10 variants, using an LLM-as-judge to run synthetic customers against an agent. Boutier ran the same agent on two models and found that one was faster and consumed fewer tokens. Boutier noted buyers are open to a speech-to-text and text-to-speech cascade, “but what they realize is that voice-to-voice models sound just better.” Cognigy now serves as both a Model Context Protocol client and server and supports agent-to-agent connections, including one customer linking Cognigy to agents built with Microsoft’s tooling. NiCE is also co-developing the Personal Agent Protocol with Meta and Sierra, which isn’t live yet.

Cognigy earned its pre-acquisition leadership position by handling complex production deployments for large brands such as Lufthansa, Mercedes and DHL. NiCE is the market leader in contact center as a service, as Cognigy was in conversational AI. Boutier said each guardrail adds tokens and latency, and “the more you add, the more bloated your agent becomes.” Boutier described Cognigy as “the front door” of the contact center, where a consumer’s personal agent must authenticate before it can proceed. Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting, and wrote the article for SiliconANGLE.

The challenge is to get an easier-to-work-with Cognigy into the hands of thousands of CXone customers without creating a sprawl of individually governed agents. Regional rules on AI disclosure and human escalation must be built in by the customer. Companies can also let personal agents work through their websites and APIs, so the front-door position depends on enterprises routing that traffic through Cognigy. There has been a wave of companies banning personal agents. The article leaves open which personal agents enterprises will accept and what they can do.

Articles.Title: NiCE's next-generation Cognigy bets the hard part of AI agents is running them, not building them

stories.Headline: EU plan for cloud and AI falls short on digital autonomy
stories.Summary:
Researchers at the Institute for Information Law at the University of Amsterdam say the EU's proposed Cloud and AI Development Act falls short of its goal of strengthening Europe's cloud and AI sectors. The proposal is intended to reduce Europe's dependence on providers from outside Europe. The European Commission proposed the act, known as CADA. The researchers also are concerned about the rapid expansion of data centers and the limited attention paid to sustainability and social impact. The analysis was published on November 13, 2026.

The European cloud market is highly dependent on three U.S. tech giants, which together control more than 70% of the market. The EU spends €264 billion a year on predominantly U.S. IT products and services. The proposal aims to make investment in large-scale data center expansion more attractive, including by reducing administrative red tape and simplifying permit requirements. It also introduces rules for public-sector procurement of cloud services. The proposal introduces four Union assurance levels, with increasingly strict requirements for cloud services.

Kristina Irion, one of the researchers, says the proposal could undermine Dutch ambitions to achieve greater digital sovereignty and reduce dependence on Big Tech, at a time when the Netherlands is taking steps in that direction. The researchers argue that the proposal would limit public authorities' ability to set additional requirements for many services and thereby reduce their dependence on a handful of third-country providers. Irion says that as currently drafted, the EU proposal could even prevent public-sector organizations from consciously choosing a European alternative. Co-author Plixavra Vogiatzoglou says that under the proposal, providers and developers from outside the EU would retain a strong foothold. Irion says greater digital autonomy also requires clear sustainability rules, democratic participation, stronger public procurement requirements and more support for European and open alternatives.

The researchers assessed the proposal across five areas: cloud and AI leadership, expanding data center capacity, digital sovereignty and public procurement, Union assurance levels, and open source and cloud federations. They say the proposal focuses too heavily on growth and AI's potential benefits, and that the effects on fundamental rights, employment, local communities and the environment receive too little attention. They also call for stronger safeguards for transparency, participation and local involvement. The researchers say sustainability and social impacts are not adequately safeguarded, and they question whether the proposal explains convincingly why data centers should take priority over other demands for energy, water, land and electricity grid capacity. Many public services would be assigned the lowest Union assurance level, which the researchers say limits public authorities' ability to set additional procurement requirements for many services.

The researchers say the criteria do not automatically exclude large U.S. providers, which may be able to meet many of the requirements at the two lower levels. The European Commission estimates that only 10% of use cases would require the highest levels, from which third-country providers are excluded. The researchers say that support for open source is limited and largely optional. They also question how organizations can share cloud services when they rent the infrastructure from a provider rather than owning it themselves. The proposal aims to speed up data center construction, including by creating special zones where permits can be issued more quickly.

Articles.Title: EU plan for cloud and AI falls short on digital autonomy

stories.Headline: Don't like AI in games? Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss ain't care: it's expanding AI use 'throughout our entire development pipeline'
stories.Summary:
Pearl Abyss said in its Q3 2026 earnings letter that it will expand its use of AI throughout its entire development pipeline, PC Gamer reported on 13 November 2026. The Crimson Desert studio made the statement midway through the letter, which Eurogamer covered. The studio had apologized earlier this year for the presence of AI-generated art in Crimson Desert. It apologized not because it had used generative AI, but because players saw it. The letter said the studio now uses AI to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation.

The letter said Pearl Abyss previously validated game systems only after implementing them manually. It said the new approach enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed. The studio said AI is being utilized across various stages of development, including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization. It said it is expanding AI implementation throughout its entire development pipeline. The studio said it views AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality.

Pearl Abyss said AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity. It said gameplay and content development remain fully driven by its development team. The studio said it is integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. It said it will continue to expand its application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously. In February, the studio acknowledged that some 2D visual props had been created by AI during the early stages of development.

The studio said those props were supposed to be replaced following final work and review by its art and development teams, with work that aligned with its quality standards and creative direction. It also admitted that it had not clearly disclosed its use of AI in the development process. The studio promised to be more transparent about it in the future. PC Gamer said the letter could be seen as a step in that direction. The article did not name any other parties affected by the change.

The February statement followed players discovering the presence of generative AI art in Crimson Desert. The studio said the AI-made 2D visual props dated to the early stages of development. It said the props were meant to be replaced after review by its art and development teams. The studio said the replacements would align with its quality standards and creative direction. It also said it had not clearly disclosed its use of AI during development.

Pearl Abyss said it will continue to expand its application of AI. The letter did not give a date for the expanded pipeline use or name specific tools. The articles did not say how players responded to the Q3 2026 letter. The articles did not give sales figures or a release date for Crimson Desert. The articles did not say whether the studio set any limits on which tasks AI may handle.

Articles.Title: Don't like AI in games? Crimson Desert studio Pearl Abyss ain't care: it's expanding AI use 'throughout our entire development pipeline'

stories.Headline: Visure Launches Visure X for AI-Assisted Requirements Management
stories.Summary:
Visure Solutions announced the general availability of Visure X on November 13, 2026. The company launched this new platform from its headquarters in San Francisco. It provides AI-assisted requirements management for organizations developing safety-critical and regulated products. The software is available now for new customers and existing Visure Requirements ALM users. This next-generation experience was rebuilt from the ground up for large and complex programs.

The platform supports aerospace, defense, automotive, medical device, rail and industrial teams in San Francisco. It integrates requirements, models, risks, tests, and the wider PLM and CAD digital thread. Templates support frameworks including DO-178C, ISO 26262, ASPICE, IEC 62304, ISO 14971, and EN 50128. Users can choose LLM providers via cloud, Microsoft Azure, Amazon Bedrock, or fully local models. Integration is enabled through ReqIF, SysML model import, webhooks, a REST API, and MCP.

Visure Solutions is a leading provider of requirements management and ALM software for regulated industries. The company stated that Visure X helps teams take products from concept to certification faster. They noted that the platform maintains the traceability and audit evidence that regulators expect. The company explained that the tool connects requirements to the wider digital thread through design. They claimed the system is significantly faster than the previous Visure Requirements ALM software.

Existing customers requested more speed on large projects, a simpler interface, and better parallel work support. Engineering organizations are under pressure to adopt AI but find generic assistants lack regulatory understanding. These teams often spend weeks reconstructing pictures by hand before every review or audit. Regulated programs are affected because generic AI output must still be checked, traced, and justified. The new system allows these teams to adopt AI within their own data-handling rules.

Safety-critical products now combine mechanical, electrical, software, and systems engineering across various suppliers and variants. Each engineering discipline typically works in its own tool, which creates fragmented information. A single requirement change can ripple into models, CAD, tests, hazard analyses, and certification evidence. Generic AI assistants do not understand an organization's specific information model, approval rules, or regulatory obligations. This environment makes it difficult to maintain a consistent digital thread during the development process.

Existing customers can contact their account managers to learn about various upgrade options for their systems. Interested parties can visit the company website at www.visuresolutions.com to request a product demonstration. Teams can move individual specifications at their own pace using a server-to-server import tool. The articles do not state the specific pricing for the new Visure X platform. They also leave open the specific timeline for future updates to the AI Agent.

Articles.Title: Visure Launches Visure X for AI-Assisted Requirements Management

stories.Headline: What the Next UN Secretary-General Should Do about AI
stories.Summary:
A new secretary-general will take office in January 2027 to address artificial intelligence risks. This leader can engage major powers on security risks and start practical diplomatic initiatives. The goal is to make AI a priority for preventive diplomacy to ensure stability. This effort follows a July 6, 2026, meeting between António Guterres and scientific experts. The new leader will act before several major international meetings scheduled for 2027.

The leader must prepare for New York meetings on May 3rd and 4th, 2027. They must also prepare for the Geneva AI Summit on June 21st and 22nd. The plan requires confidential consultations with China, the United States, and other militarily powerful states. It suggests a voluntary protocol for communication when AI incidents threaten to escalate international tensions. A tabletop exercise could simulate how officials respond to misleading AI warnings during crises.

Martin Wählisch suggests the secretary-general should use the office to sustain engagement on risks. He believes the leader should establish regular briefings for the Security Council on AI. Wählisch argues that the first 100 days are critical for setting a focused agenda. He states that personal engagement is valuable for identifying where governments can reach agreements. He notes that modest progress could prevent misunderstandings during a time of geopolitical tension.

The Security Council has discussed AI effects on nuclear stability, cybersecurity, and military decision making. Member states are affected by the risk of AI agents going rogue or malfunctioning. Civil society groups are mentioned as partners for conversations on the impact of AI. The Independent International Scientific Panel on AI provides findings on emerging capabilities and risks. These scientific conclusions should inform diplomatic discussions beyond the usual specialist technical forums.

The UN Office for Disarmament Affairs and UN Institute for Disarmament Research have studied military AI. The Department of Peace Operations and Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs engage with emerging technologies. The Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies provides perspectives on governance and scientific research. These efforts occur as the peace and security architecture evolves under the UN80 reform initiative. The 81st General Assembly session focuses on restoring trust and managing global transformation.

The new leader will ask for closer cooperation between personnel in technology and disarmament. They will engage co-chairs of the Global Dialogue and organizers of the Swiss summit. The leader may seek options for sharing technical capacities, scientific expertise, and computing resources. The articles leave open whether governments will actually agree to these practical arrangements. It remains uncertain if promises will translate into actions that reduce risks to peace.

Articles.Title: What the Next UN Secretary-General Should Do about AI

stories.Headline: Twelfth annual Emerson-Blanquerna summit discusses AI preparedness in the communication sphere
stories.Summary:
Dozens of Emerson College students, faculty, staff, and alumni attended a summit last month. The twelfth annual Emerson-Blanquerna Global Communication Summit took place on October 30, 2026. Participants gathered in Washington, D.C. to learn leadership skills and discuss artificial intelligence. The event focused on how AI is upending the future of work and communication. Over half a dozen speakers who attended Emerson during the past five decades participated.

The summit occurred at the global headquarters of Vital Voices in Washington, D.C. This women's leadership organization was co-founded by Emerson Trustee Alyse Nelson '97. The event featured speakers including Peter Loge '87, Patrick Morris '97, and Lee Schwebel '90. Other speakers were Lee Stacey '76, Fred Baldassaro '96, Susan del Percio '90, Rael Ammon '08, and Grant Cos. The summit brought together educators from the United States, Spain, Portugal, Slovenia, China, Nepal, and Ghana.

Dr. Gregory Payne co-founded the Emerson-Blanquerna Center for Global Communication in 2014 and gave opening remarks. He stated that holding summits in D.C. helps grow the footprint of Emerson in the capital. President Jay Bernhardt said that effective communication requires expertise and stories that resonate with people's values. Bernhardt argued that communicators must stop talking and start listening to be effective in a polarized society. He noted that democracy requires leaders to tell inclusive stories to everyone, not just their own side.

USA TODAY Bureau Chief Susan Page called artificial intelligence the newest disruption for journalists. She believes young journalists have an advantage because these tools will be native to them. Page expressed concern regarding the erosion of trust between journalists and their audiences. Lluc Vila Boix, who earned a Ph.D. from Blanquerna, praised the genuine connection between the two institutions. Visiting schools included Howard University, George Washington University, University of Washington, and Hong Kong Baptist University.

The Emerson-Blanquerna Center is a partnership with the Blanquerna School of Communication and International Relations in Barcelona, Spain. Since its start, the center has hosted annual summits in Boston, Barcelona, or Washington, D.C. These events typically bring together more than 130 students, faculty, alumni, and special guests. Alyse Nelson recalled attending the 1995 World Conference on Women in Beijing as an undergraduate student. There, she heard First Lady Hillary Clinton state that women's rights are human rights.

In Spring 2027, more than a dozen AI-adjacent courses will be taught across various college departments. These courses aim to ensure students are AI-fluent regardless of the industry they enter. Bernhardt stated that human intention must guide technological possibility and that story comes first. The articles do not state how many students will enroll in these specific AI courses. They also leave open how journalists will specifically regain the trust of their audiences.

Articles.Title: Twelfth annual Emerson-Blanquerna summit discusses AI preparedness in the communication sphere

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang officially stepped down as the CEO of Nvidia on November 13, 2026. He had co-founded and led the company for 33 years before his resignation. This departure has caused significant alarm among venture capitalists and startup founders. Many describe the news as a sudden shock to the artificial intelligence ecosystem.

The change affects a company that participated in 105 funding rounds this year alone. Nvidia previously spent billions on startups, including a $13 billion purchase of Hugging Face expected to close in 2027. The firm also provided $800 million for a $2 billion round for Reflection AI last year. Other major investments included a $1.4 billion Series E for Crusoe and backing for Mistral AI, Lambda, and Black Forest Labs.

Interim CEO Colette Kress is now responsible for the company's direction. Investors describe her as more conservative than Huang and expect her to reduce spending on early-stage companies. Some believe she will be more selective with new investments and write smaller checks for existing ones. This shift may lower startup valuations and leave a funding gap in regions like Europe.

The previous investment strategy helped Nvidia maintain a dominant market position by locking startups into its CUDA software platform. Some experts hope that rivals like Google, Amazon, Microsoft, or AMD will fill the void. However, others doubt these competitors will provide the same level of funding for pre-revenue infrastructure. The industry now waits to see if the broader AI boom can survive without Huang's aggressive dealmaking.

Articles.Title: Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say

stories.Headline: Siri AI Still Not Enabled on HomePod Mini 2 With Latest Software Update
stories.Summary:
Apple released HomePod software version 27.2.1 on Friday, November 13, 2026, according to MacRumors, but the update does not enable Siri AI on the HomePod mini 2. The report was published by Joe Rossignol at 12:18 pm PST that day. Apple also released tvOS 27.2.1 the same day. That update enables Siri AI on the Apple TV 4K (2nd generation) and the Apple TV 4K (3rd generation). The HomePod mini 2 still lacks the feature after the new software.

Apple's website continues to say Siri AI is "coming in a future software update," but Apple has not provided a timeframe. The HomePod mini 2 has only 2GB of RAM, well below the minimum 8GB of RAM required for dedicated Siri AI. Because of that limit, personal context requests on the HomePod mini 2 will require a paired Apple Intelligence, enabled iPhone or iPad with Siri AI turned on. Siri AI is an opt-in feature on the Apple TV 4K models, so after installing tvOS 27.2.1 you must open the Settings app and tap General, then Siri, then Siri AI (Beta). That step initiates a download with support.

If you update to tvOS 27.2.1 and take no further action, Siri Classic remains enabled by default. The MacRumors article carries a related roundup for the HomePod mini 2 and tags for the Siri Guide and Siri AI. It also links a buyer's guide for the HomePod Mini with a Buy Now option. The article points readers to a related forum for HomePod, HomeView and CarPlay under Home & Auto Tech. The page shows 38 comments on the story.

Commenters on the article questioned the rollout, with one calling the Siri AI rollout inconsistent and another writing that the release "made zero sense." One commenter wrote that the feature is "coming on Febutober the eleventeenth." Another said it would be good if a senior Apple executive were asked about this sort of thing in an interview rather than a promotional piece. One commenter said Apple was already subject of a class action lawsuit about Apple Intelligence and that selling hardware on vague or delayed promises of functionality wastes your brand. Another commenter said turning the feature on would improve sales of Google Home speakers.

MacRumors also reported that HomePod Software 27.2 adds a Sound Glow feature to the HomePod, HomePod mini and HomePod mini 2. Apple introduced Sound Glow as a HomePod mini 2 feature, but it is available for the second-generation HomePod and the original HomePod mini too. HomePod Software 27.2 was available as a release candidate update for developers and public beta testers. MacRumors also reported that iOS 27.2 and iPadOS 27.2, released on Monday, October 26, 2026, expanded Siri AI to new languages. The site's upcoming calendar lists Apple HomeView and Apple TV, both with Siri AI support, as launching November 13.

The MacRumors article does not say when, or whether, Siri AI will arrive on the HomePod mini 2. It gives no date for the "future software update" Apple's website mentions. It does not state how personal context requests will work on the HomePod mini 2 without a paired device. It does not say whether Siri AI on the HomePod mini 2 will also be opt-in. The article does not report any Apple comment on the missing feature beyond the website wording.

Articles.Title: Siri AI Still Not Enabled on HomePod Mini 2 With Latest Software Update

stories.Headline: Road to AI ICON webinar series prepares Central Texas professionals for 2027 conference
stories.Summary:
AI ICON 2027 organizers are bringing artificial intelligence education to business owners, entrepreneurs and professionals through the “Road to AI ICON” webinar series, an initiative designed to help participants turn emerging technology into practical business solutions. The Innovative Black Chamber of Commerce organized the series, and AI ICON 2027 is being planned for next year in Killeen. The upcoming webinar series focuses on real-world applications of artificial intelligence, including business automation, software development, client management and digital productivity. The online sessions are intended to provide accessible training for individuals seeking to incorporate AI into their daily operations, regardless of their technical background. One featured webinar, “Building a Webapp Portal for Your Clients,” is led by Divine Devon and demonstrates how participants can use OpenAI’s Codex technology to create digital platforms without extensive programming experience.

The training covers the development of client dashboards, assessment forms and private online portals, allowing businesses to organize information, manage customer relationships and monitor client progress. The webinar is particularly relevant to consultants, coaches, brokers and other service-based professionals interested in reducing administrative workloads and improving customer communication. The Road to AI ICON webinar listing identifies an online session held Oct. 22, 2026, from 11 a.m. to noon. The listing describes the series as an opportunity for both beginners and experienced users to explore AI developments ahead of the conference.

AI ICON 2027 is scheduled for February 2027 at the Killeen Civic and Conference Center. The educational series also serves as a lead-up to AI ICON 2027, a Central Texas conference centered on artificial intelligence, innovation and professional development. Under the theme “From Prompt to Action,” the conference will emphasize moving beyond basic AI-generated responses toward developing automated workflows, digital products and practical technology solutions. The IBCC is preparing educational opportunities for participants at different experience levels, from beginners exploring artificial intelligence for the first time to professionals seeking more advanced applications. The initiative highlights the increasing importance of artificial intelligence literacy as businesses explore new ways to improve efficiency, expand services and remain competitive in a changing technological environment.

The 2027 conference is expected to expand on the previous year’s event with beginner and intermediate tracks and advanced workshops covering autonomous AI agents, natural-language software development, AI memory and context engineering, and multimedia creation involving video, audio and interactive 3D technology. Conference organizers emphasize hands-on participation rather than traditional presentations, with attendees expected to bring fully charged laptops to complete practical exercises. The conference and webinar initiative aim to equip Central Texas professionals with practical skills as artificial intelligence continues to influence business operations, education and workforce development. The final schedule has not yet been released.

Articles.Title: Road to AI ICON webinar series prepares Central Texas professionals for 2027 conference

stories.Headline: OpenAI Gives AI Agents a Wallet While Blocking Them From Seeing the Card
stories.Summary:
OpenAI introduced a ChatGPT Wallet on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026, according to a company press release. The wallet lets AI agents make purchases without seeing users' card details. It requires a security check for every purchase. It also keeps existing card rewards and protections in place.

The wallet will first be available through OpenAI's personal AI agents, called dots, for ChatGPT Pro subscribers. Those users must be 18 or older, live in the United States, and have an eligible U.S.-issued card. OpenAI built the wallet with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. OpenAI said 1.2 billion people use ChatGPT each week, and many use it to research products, compare options and decide what to buy.

To pay, users add a card once and review each purchase's items, total and selected card. They then approve the purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. After approval, the payment network provides a payment token, and the card is charged without the card details being shared with the business or the agent. OpenAI said it plans to let users delegate purchases entirely to their agents over time, with clear parameters, preapprovals and stronger safeguards.

OpenAI also published a Commerce Partner Playbook to help businesses adapt to agentic commerce. It explains how businesses can make product information available, ensure agent access, and work with payment and risk providers to reduce unnecessary declines. OpenAI said it will work with businesses, banks and payment networks to learn from early use and expand availability. A PYMNTS Intelligence report found consumers are comfortable letting AI tools handle research but much less comfortable delegating identity, payment choice or an irreversible decision.

Articles.Title: OpenAI Gives AI Agents a Wallet While Blocking Them From Seeing the Card

stories.Headline: Costco Trusts AI to Reorder Drugs. Most Retailers Won’t
stories.Summary:
Costco's pharmacy inventory system now uses artificial intelligence to compare prescription drug prices across vendors and reorder inventory on its own, CEO Ron Vachris said on the company's fiscal first-quarter 2026 earnings call on Dec. 11, 2025. The system reorders predictively, before shelves run low, and lifted in-stock levels above 98%, Vachris said. He said it played an important role in mid-teen growth in prescriptions filled and improved margins and member prices, though he gave no figures for either. CFO Gary Millerchip said in March on the fiscal second-quarter 2026 call that Costco had added new AI tools to improve pharmacy in-stock positions.

Costco is also deploying AI tools in its gasoline business, which Vachris said should improve inventory management and drive incremental sales. The final five weeks of fiscal third-quarter 2026 were Costco's top five gas volume weeks ever, requiring multiple daily deliveries at many locations, he said on May 28. On Sept. 24, Vachris said prescriptions filled grew double digits in fiscal 2026 and pharmacy sales grew nearly 20%, crediting GLP-1 and fertility programs, pickup lockers and Rx Mobile Pay Ahead, with more than one-third of prescriptions at many U.S. warehouses paid ahead. He said the growth more than offset lower prices from Medicare maximum fair price changes, and that when Costco sees lower prices it sees an opportunity, pointing to lower GLP-1 prices driving unit growth. Costco has not detailed AI's impact on pharmacy growth.

Most retailers are not ready to let AI place orders on its own. A July PYMNTS Intelligence report, based on a survey of 60 senior technology executives at U.S. enterprises with at least $1 billion in annual revenue, found that 90% of retail firms would limit an AI agent to look-up access and 5% would allow some execution with human approval. Sixty percent said their main five-year goal is semi-autonomous AI with human oversight, and no executive surveyed expects fully autonomous AI within five years. Sixty-five percent of wholesale and retail firms plan to raise AI budgets over the next 12 months, and 40% of retail firms expect a return within one to two years.

Articles.Title: Costco Trusts AI to Reorder Drugs. Most Retailers Won’t

stories.Headline: Kevin Simpson Is Buying More Caterpillar as an AI Trade That Isn’t Just AI
stories.Summary:
Kevin Simpson added to his Caterpillar (NYSE:CAT) position after a steep slide, saying in a CNBC Trade Tracker segment on November 13, 2026 that he is buying more shares. He said he and his team looked at Caterpillar as an adjacent trade to the AI. He called it probably a stock that moved far too fast, too far, but has come down dramatically. Caterpillar trades near $595.96, down 22.7% over the past month from $770.96 and roughly 44% below its 52-week high of $1,068.93. It sits under both its 50-day average of $752.06 and its 200-day average of $808.13, and a 7.64% bounce over the past week leaves shares up just 4.92% year to date.

Generation revenue rose 30% to $3.421 billion in the third quarter, after gains of 44%, 41% and 29% in the prior three quarters, and power generation sales to users jumped 75%. Backlog hit a record $78 billion, up 96% from a year earlier, with large engine orders stretching to 2029 and turbine orders into 2030. Construction Industries revenue grew 18% to $7.983 billion, and Resource Industries rose 15% to $4.615 billion on copper, gold, and Canadian oil sands demand, while Oil and Gas added 13% on gas compression. Total revenue reached $20.68 billion, and adjusted EPS of $7.20 topped the $7.04 consensus, per the third-quarter earnings release filed with the SEC.

Chief Executive Joe Creed said on the call that what the company hears from customers is they still want more if Caterpillar can get them more power. Creed noted that data centers have a little bit of a rollover into CI as well. Creed admitted there is no slack in the system after a test cell outage. Simpson said it is not just an AI trade, adding that there is also mining and industrial, and a lot there.

On CNBC's Fast Money, Steve Grasso described money rotating into defensives, saying Caterpillar is down 30 and semiconductors down 30. Caterpillar trades at a trailing P/E of 23 and a forward multiple of 18, and the quarterly dividend of $1.63 annualizes to $6.52, a yield near 1.1%. The company bought back $1.2 billion of stock in the quarter, and analysts lean positive with 2 Strong Buy, 15 Buy, 11 Hold and 1 Sell ratings and an average target of $823.41. Tariff costs are expected around $2.2 billion for 2026, keeping margins near the bottom of the target range, and Resource Industries sales to users grew only 4%, below expectations, on shipping and setup delays. A beta of 1.64 means the stock moves harder than the market when construction or commodity cycles turn.

Management plans to discuss 2027 around the fourth-quarter earnings report, and the article says to watch whether backlog keeps climbing and margins lift off the bottom of the range. The article says the past month shows the catch: when AI sentiment cracks, Caterpillar falls alongside semiconductors. The article says Caterpillar's AI exposure is physical, backed by a multiyear backlog, and layered on top of mining, construction, and gas compression businesses that grow on their own. The article says chip stocks offer purer AI leverage, while Caterpillar offers more ways to win.

Articles.Title: Kevin Simpson Is Buying More Caterpillar as an AI Trade That Isn’t Just AI

stories.Headline: AI Positively Associates With High-Quality Development in Chinese Listed Pharmaceutical Firms
stories.Summary:
Researchers at Shenyang Pharmaceutical University conducted a study on the impact of artificial intelligence. They analyzed data from pharmaceutical companies listed on the Shenzhen and Shanghai A-share markets. This investigation covered the period between 2007 and 2024. The team found that using AI is strongly linked to high-quality development in these firms.

The study used an empirical index to measure firm performance and progress. It found that AI helps overcome long-term issues like high research costs and low success rates. The positive results remained consistent after using propensity score matching and lagged explanatory variables. The researchers also used an instrumental-variable estimation strategy to confirm their findings. This correlation held true regardless of ownership structures or regional environments.

The authors, Y. Zhu, Q. Liu, and Y. Chen, identified two main ways AI helps these companies. They noted that AI adoption helps firms gain more government subsidies and policy resources. They also found that AI use is linked to a higher number of highly skilled employees. The authors stated that these findings offer practical guidance for corporate technology strategies. They believe AI can help relieve industrial bottlenecks in the sector.

The pharmaceutical industry is considered a strategic sector for public health and economic stability. The study showed that mature firms and those in central and western China saw larger benefits. These results suggest that AI integration can improve the resilience of public health systems. The researchers concluded that these insights can help officials design better public policies. This approach aims to support the overall growth of pharmaceutical manufacturing.

Articles.Title: AI Positively Associates With High-Quality Development in Chinese Listed Pharmaceutical Firms

stories.Headline: India pins hopes on AI start-up to avoid becoming ‘digital colony’
stories.Summary:
The Financial Times published a headline on 13 November 2026 saying India is pinning its hopes on an AI start-up to avoid becoming a “digital colony”. The article itself is behind a paywall, so the body of the story is not available. The headline is the only substantive information the article provides. No details are given about which start-up is involved or what it has done. The available text does not say what the start-up requires or what would change.

It gives no numbers, dates or names beyond the publication date of 13 November 2026. The only figure shown is the subscription pricing for the FT, which is not part of the story. The article does not name any officials, companies or investors. Because the article is locked, it is not possible to say who is responsible or what anyone said.

The headline suggests the effort is tied to India’s concerns about dependence on foreign technology, but the article does not explain this. No statements from the start-up, the government or anyone else are included in the accessible text. The context and next steps are therefore unknown. More to follow.

Articles.Title: India pins hopes on AI start-up to avoid becoming ‘digital colony’

stories.Headline: Island launches enterprise browser to control AI agents
stories.Summary:
Island launched an Enterprise Browser for Agents on 13 November 2026, according to IT Brief Australia. The software lets AI agents use software-as-a-service tools, internal applications and public websites while working under enterprise policies. Island says the product extends the browser controls already used for human employees to software agents that browse, read and act across systems. Businesses are starting to use agents for routine work such as updating customer records, onboarding staff and processing invoices.

The controls apply at the browser activity level rather than to the agents themselves, and Island says end users and agents cannot disable or bypass them. Policy can set permissions by agent and by application, define which document object model operations are allowed, and decide whether an agent can write or only read. Agents inherit the user's identity and permissions, and policy can apply to the user alone, to the user and agent together, or to the agent separately. Logs record whether a human or an agent took an action, and sessions can be recorded for visual playback of pages, clicks and form submissions.

A read-only mode lets agents extract information from systems such as enterprise resource planning platforms without changing, submitting or deleting data. Dan Amiga, Chief Technology Officer and Co-founder at Island, said the company already had what agents need, including identity federation, data boundaries, credential isolation and full attribution, all proven in production. He said agents inherit Island's security model from day one, with policies built specifically for them. He also said that within a few years most enterprises' browser activity will come from agents rather than people, and that organisations treating agent browsing as a separate problem end up running a second workforce nobody can see.

The launch comes as technology suppliers race to define how AI agents should operate inside corporate systems. Island argues that many organisations have relied on patchwork arrangements built on consumer browser infrastructure, which it says can create risks around credentials, data handling and changes to records. The browser can be deployed on devices and in the cloud, covering local and remote agents without a cloud-hosted browser running outside the customer's environment. Island says it helped define the enterprise browser category and has applied the same policy framework used for human workers to this new product.

Articles.Title: Island launches enterprise browser to control AI agents - IT Brief Australia

stories.Headline: Why structured business data is becoming more important in an AI-driven economy
stories.Summary:
Petersen Zhu wrote an article on November 13, 2026, about structured business data. The piece explains why this data is becoming more important in an AI-driven economy. It discusses how AI agents can now become the backbone of e-commerce operations. These tools help businesses cut expenses, streamline operations, and reduce human error. The report highlights the necessity of clean inputs for automating complex business workflows.

Digital readiness requires unified data infrastructure and clean business data across all sales channels. It also needs interoperability and automation to reduce manual human intervention to a minimum. B2C retailers may use Shopify, WooCommerce, Amazon, eBay, Walmart, TikTok Shop, Instagram, and warehouse management systems. Wholesalers manage master cartons, case packs, pallet configurations, custom contract pricing, and rigid EDI feeds. These entities operate across B2B portals, legacy ERPs, wholesale marketplaces, and manual sales entries.

DigitBridge, a unified commerce platform, explains that AI agents need clean, unified inputs. They state that AI cannot recognize patterns or automate workflows without structured business data. The company notes that e-commerce operations have no physical substrate like traditional brick-and-mortar shops. DigitBridge argues that businesses break if their data is wrong, disconnected, or out of sync. They suggest that a unified platform provides the execution layer AI agents need.

Multi-channel retailers lose 5 percent to 15 percent of annual revenue to operational errors. These losses come from stockouts and overselling caused by fragmented data across different channels. B2C customers are affected by canceled orders and poor experiences when stock is oversold. Wholesale clients face broken supply chain compliance and misrouted bulk inventory due to sync failures. Corporate contracts can be cancelled when multi-tiered data hierarchies fail to align across systems.

Gartner predicted that over 80 percent of enterprises would use generative AI by 2026. Most popular generative AI platforms were originally built for unstructured data like text and images. E-commerce businesses often skipped foundational data steps before AI-powered tools became widely available. Retailers often use non-standardized structures for SKUs, prices, quantities, and customer IDs across platforms. This fragmentation creates mismatched workflows that previously required human employees to manage manually.

Allen said that with the power of AI, BuzzFeed is officially chasing YouTube to become another premiere free video streaming service. stories.Headline: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training
stories.Summary:
Researchers at a United States medical school conducted a pilot study on AI patient simulations. The team tested these encounters with first-year medical students in November 2026. They wanted to see if large language models could be used for clinical training. The study compared two different ways of delivering the simulation. All participants completed the assigned tasks without any total technical failures.

The project involved 19 students recruited from a pool of 72, which was a 26 percent rate. Seven students were placed in a facilitated group, while 12 worked in a self-paced individual format. The group session lasted about 35 minutes, and the individual sessions had a median length of 31 minutes. Researchers used the Behavioral Safety Language Scale-Provisional to measure student perceptions. Most students, or 58 percent, preferred a hybrid model of working alone first and then in a group.

Shelley Tischkau, James Lynch, Sean McGinity, Andrew Primous, Elijah Meldrim, Samantha Lynch, and Richard Selinfreund led the investigation. They noted that the simulation was feasible and received favorable ratings from the students. However, the authors stated that the results are exploratory and do not prove educational effectiveness. They explained that the data must be confirmed with a larger, randomized sample. The team also mentioned that some students experienced intermittent technical problems.

This research fits into a broader effort to use generative AI for case-based and problem-based learning. Current medical education research often lacks specific details on delivery formats and outcome measurements. This pilot study attempted to fill those gaps by testing distinct learning environments. The researchers used Wilcoxon signed-rank exact tests and the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to analyze the data. Future studies will be needed to determine if these tools actually improve medical training.

Articles.Title: Pilot Tests Show Feasibility of AI Patient Simulations in Medical Training

The agency provides emergency call handling and communications infrastructure throughout Grant County. They currently use AI for quality assurance and simulated calls for training. stories.Headline: NBIS Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on AI Cloud Growth, Asset-Light Gains

Nebius Group N.V. reported third-quarter 2026 results on November 13, 2026, with adjusted earnings of 30 cents per share against an adjusted loss of about 42 cents a year earlier, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of a 61-cent loss. Revenue rose 571% year over year to $980.8 million, above the $917 million consensus. AI Cloud revenue was $973.8 million, up 643% and about 99% of consolidated revenue, and annualized run-rate revenue reached $6.4 billion, up 1,062%. The quarter included roughly $325 million in nonrecurring revenue from the first phase of an asset-light model in which partners fund computing capacity while Nebius provides its architecture and cloud platform.

Remaining performance obligations were $38.7 billion at the end of September, up 3% sequentially, and customers committed more than $12 billion in total contract value since the start of the third quarter. Annual contract value per megawatt exceeded $25 million, compared with $20 million to $25 million in the prior quarter, and average GPU-hour pricing rose more than 20% sequentially. More than 90% of contract value signed in the quarter included customer prepayments, which covered more than 100% of associated capital expenditures, compared with 50% to 60% in the second quarter, and the average payback period shortened to one year and seven months from one year and 10 months. Nebius also signed multiyear agreements with Databricks, Datadog and Snowflake, and its Token Factory platform neared a multi-hundred-million-dollar annual revenue run rate, with contract value up 17 times sequentially.

Adjusted EBITDA was $465.8 million against a loss of $5.2 million a year earlier, and the margin improved to 47.5% from 40.6% in the second quarter, with the AI Cloud business at 53.2%. Total operating costs and expenses rose 237% to $930.4 million, and capital expenditures were about $7.3 billion. Nebius ended September with $7.43 billion in cash and equivalents, a net loss from continuing operations of $37.5 million, and net cash used in operating activities of $273 million. During the quarter it completed a $5.75 billion convertible senior notes offering, secured a $775 million asset-backed financing facility and raised about $1 billion in net proceeds through an at-the-market equity offering.

Nebius now expects 2026 revenue of $3 billion to $3.2 billion, down from $3 billion to $3.4 billion, citing delays in bringing third-party data center capacity online, particularly in New Jersey. It kept its full-year adjusted EBITDA margin expectation at about 40% but raised projected capital expenditures to around $27 billion from $20 billion to $25 billion. For 2027, management expects revenue of $12 billion to $13 billion, capital expenditures of $40 billion to $45 billion with 75% to 85% financed through customer prepayments and asset-backed financing, customer prepayments of $17 billion to $20 billion, and pretax breakeven in the fourth quarter of 2027. stories.Headline: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model
stories.Summary:
Over the last month, AI penetration testing and orchestration frameworks have exploded in number. These tools automate offensive security workflows to carry out the Cyber Kill Chain at scale. Many of these frameworks are based on an open source system called ARTEX. The creator of ARTEX, Autumn-27, took the original tool down on October 8. Since then, fragmented versions and similar agentic orchestration frameworks have proliferated.

The Modern Security Model requires a WAF with rate limits and anomaly detection on all web applications. It calls for Bot Defense and Identity-Gated Access for high-risk external and internal web applications. Organizations must enforce validated schemas, explicit security controls, and implement Threat Intelligence. Cloudflare observed over 50 framework families scanning customers globally in just three days. Thousands of IP addresses have been seen running these tools.

Cloudforce One is responsible for tracking these threats and investigating incident responses. They stated that these autonomous agents represent a doctrinal shift in offensive cyber capabilities. The team noted that human skills are no longer the limiting factor in attacks. They explained that these tools turn compromises into a hill-climbable problem for agents. They recommended that every organization adopt the six pillars of the Modern Security Model.

Defenders are struggling to keep up with the volumetric nature of these autonomously guided attacks. Some threat actors have used stolen customer credentials to perform lateral movement throughout environments. These attackers compromised static, non-expiring tokens running inside CI/CD pipelines to gain broad access. One incident involved a compromise originating through a third-party hyperscaler. This allowed the actor to pivot directly into a customer's Cloudflare environment.

ARTEX and its forks make up over 60 percent of known AI penetration testing orchestrators. Daily requests for these exploitation tools grew 30x since October 1. There are now over 12,000 repositories, including several hundred unique forks of the original ARTEX. Five popular autonomous orchestrators include ARTEX, LuaN1aoAgent, Decepticon, Cairn, and PentestGPT-Agent. These tools can map assets onto a graph to attack at the speed of inference.

Cloudflare expects these AI frameworks to continue to proliferate across the internet. Organizations must prepare to address the threat by implementing the suggested security pillars. One observed attack saw 400 database dump requests in an hour and 69 requests per minute. The tools also attempted persistence mechanisms and validated session tokens for other third-party applications. The articles leave open how these tools will evolve beyond current orchestration capabilities.

Articles.Title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model

stories.Headline: AI Support Improves Human Forward Roll Scoring Accuracy in Motor Skills Test
stories.Summary:
Researchers published a study in BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation on November 14, 2026. They developed an artificial intelligence model to evaluate children performing the forward roll. This AI system acted as an assessment aid for human scorers. It aimed to replicate expert consensus decisions on movement performances. The model demonstrated substantial to almost perfect agreement with expert ratings.

The study used the Fundamental Motor Skills in Sport system and 66 video recordings. These videos covered a full range of total scores from 0 to 5. Twenty raters from Malta and Poland assessed two sets of 22 videos each. Cohen's kappa values for individual criteria ranged between 0.73 and 0.85. The quadratic weighted kappa for aggregate performance reached 0.95.

The research team included Makaruk, Decelis, Makaruk, Tomaszewski, and Sadowski. They stated that low motor skill proficiency in children creates an urgent need for dependable evaluation. The authors noted that AI could alleviate practical constraints in movement instruction. They claimed the AI reduced human scoring error and boosted inter-rater reliability. They also found that AI support reduced the perceived effort of raters.

The raters were master's degree students rather than seasoned education professionals. These students experienced a mean absolute error of 0.68 with AI support. Without AI, the mean absolute error for these students rose to 0.99. The quadratic weighted kappa rose from 0.60 without support to 0.79 with support. Nineteen out of twenty raters saw a reduction in their scoring error.

The study used the NASA Task Load Index to track subjective workload. A Wilcoxon test confirmed the error reduction with a p-value under 0.001. The Holm correction method was used to adjust for multiple workload comparisons. Perceived effort showed a significant reduction with a p-value of 0.045. The researchers used a counterbalanced experimental trial to measure cognitive demand.

Future validation is required among practicing physical education teachers in school environments. The system must be tested across broader pediatric age groups and diverse motor skills. Researchers need to move beyond the forward roll to other movements. The articles leave open how the AI performs in unconstrained settings. Further study is needed to generalize these results to professional educators.

Articles.Title: AI Support Improves Human Forward Roll Scoring Accuracy in Motor Skills Test
