stories.Headline: How Nvidia used a "scorched earth, adversarial attitude" targeting proponents of export controls in DC, invoking Trump's name to get license approvals expedited (Semafor)
stories.Summary:
In January, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter told government officials that Donald Trump and Jensen Huang wanted export license approvals expedited. Teter claimed he was with the president when the two men discussed the matter and insisted the process go fast. Nvidia used an adversarial attitude to target proponents of export controls and critics of the company in Washington. The chipmaker wielded an unprecedented level of influence to shape guidelines with global security and business implications for the industry. Teter regularly invoked the name of President Trump to push the agenda of the company through the government.

Nvidia objected to proposed license conditions for H200 chips to China, calling the cloud-customer requirement a poison pill. The company wanted know-your-customer checks to apply only to buyers purchasing tens of thousands of chips, worth billions of dollars. Teter pushed for end-of-life conditions to apply only to chips facing export controls in the United States. Nvidia told staffers that a location verification provision in the 2025 Chip Security Act was not technically feasible. The company later launched a location verification technology feature in May after demonstrating it privately for several months.

Tim Teter and Jensen Huang are described by a former official as having a scorched earth, adversarial attitude. Teter accused officials of misrepresenting products and policies, insisting that they carry out the agenda of President Trump. A Bureau of Industry and Security spokesperson said it is routine for agencies to work with individual companies. This spokesperson stated that Nvidia went through the same process as any other license applicant with non-political experts. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told the All-In podcast that he would help Huang have easy access to the president.

Congressional staffers said Nvidia used gaslighting and capitalized on a lack of technical expertise to water down various bills. Former staffers claimed the company lied about cyber vulnerabilities to argue against the 2025 Chip Security Act. Bloomberg reported that Nvidia undercounted Megaspeed sales to the government by 50,000 chips, which are worth billions of dollars. The Information reported that companies tied to suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang bought at least 7.5 billion dollars in chips. A former State Department official said they weighed blacklisting Megaspeed as early as the spring of 2025.

Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia and served as CEO until he stepped down following reports of affairs with subordinates and a customer. The customer is suspected of being a Chinese spy, and the company became the world's most valuable firm. Huang developed a close relationship with Donald Trump, who viewed the company as crucial to his economic aspirations. Former AI czar David Sacks and Howard Lutnick were also key allies for the company in Washington. The company's GPUs sparked the modern AI era, and the US holds a nine-to-one compute advantage over China.

The departure of Jensen Huang has shaved 1.5 trillion dollars off the market value of the company. Many people in Washington are relishing the downfall of the former CEO after his aggressive lobbying tactics. The company declined to comment on the location-verification technology or the reports regarding its Washington influence. It remains unclear who started leaking news regarding the affair between Huang and the suspected Chinese spy. The relationship between Nvidia and government officials may become a defining scandal of the current presidency.

stories.Headline: Unstructured Data Governance: A missing foundation for agentic AI at scale
stories.Summary:
Gustavo Espinosa, Head of Data & AI at NTT DATA International Clients USA, NTT DATA, Inc., published an article on November 10, 2026, titled Unstructured Data Governance: A missing foundation for agentic AI at scale. The article appeared on nttdata.com and was also dated 10 November 2026 in a second version. It says generative AI and now agentic AI are pushing organizations beyond databases and analytical datasets into unstructured enterprise data and content. That content includes documents, presentations, emails, contracts, policies, conversations, images, audio and video. The article says most of this content was never created or managed with AI consumption in mind.

The article says enterprise data governance has focused for years on structured data such as tables, fields, models, lineage, quality rules, access controls and ownership. It says the principles remain but the capabilities must evolve, and that organizations still need ownership, metadata, quality, lineage, security, retention and accountability. It says a customer table has fields, while a contract has clauses, dates, entities and obligations that first need to be extracted and understood. It says an AI pipeline may convert a document into text, divide it into chunks, create embeddings and place those representations into a retrieval index, requiring controls to propagate across every derived representation. It says an audio recording may need transcription and speaker identification before its meaning becomes machine-usable.

The article says traditional cataloging evolves into repository discovery and content inventory, and data profiling expands into OCR, transcription, parsing and multimodal inspection. It says classification expands into topic, entity and sensitivity detection, and lineage extends beyond systems and datasets into documents, chunks, embeddings and AI responses. It says data quality expands beyond completeness and validity into readability, structural integrity, semantic consistency, extraction accuracy and relevance to the intended AI use case. It says the goal is to transform fragmented enterprise content into information assets that are discoverable, understandable, trusted, protected and reusable. It says governance must answer not only whether information can be accessed but whether it should be used, for what purpose, by whom or by what agent, and under what conditions.

The article describes a continuous operating model with visibility, understanding, control and qualification, and activation. It says visibility covers what content exists, where it resides and who owns it, and understanding covers parsing, transcribing, segmenting and enriching content. It says control and qualification apply metadata, classification, quality rules, retention, access controls and AI-use criteria, and activation makes governed content available through search, analytics, RAG, assistants and agents. It says policies need to be executable and continuously enforced rather than documented separately and applied manually after the fact. It says governance becomes embedded in the flow of information itself.

The article says enterprises moving toward AI agents need a persistent enterprise context layer called the Company Brain, which is not simply an enterprise search engine or a collection of documents connected to an LLM. It says outdated documents lead agents to reason over outdated context, and conflicting versions without clear authority may lead agents to select the wrong source. It says permissions not carried into AI retrieval may let an agent expose information the user could never access directly, and missing semantics may let an agent retrieve the right words while misunderstanding their meaning. It says absent provenance leaves organizations unable to explain which information influenced a response or action. It says unstructured data governance is one component of a broader enterprise context governance discipline ensuring knowledge is current, understandable, traceable, protected and accountable.

The article says a chatbot that retrieves an incorrect policy may produce an incorrect answer, while an agent may use that same policy to initiate a workflow, modify a system or recommend an action. It says NTT DATA has been working with assets and accelerators that evaluate unstructured content across semantic quality, visual and structural quality, and compliance and risk, producing a quantitative assessment and a disposition that acts as an AI-readiness gate. It says a policy may say sensitive customer information must be protected, a standard defines that content as restricted, a machine-readable rule applies that classification, a control masks the content and prevents unauthorized retrieval, and evidence records what was detected and enforced. It says organizations that succeed with agentic AI will be those that turn enterprise information into trusted, governed and machine-usable context. It directs readers to read more about NTT DATA's AI services to learn how to operationalize AI throughout their organization.

Articles.Title: Unstructured Data Governance: A missing foundation for agentic AI at scale - NTT Data

stories.Headline: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
stories.Summary:
Cisco Talos is tracking the growing usage of AI enabled penetration testing frameworks. These tools automate reconnaissance and vulnerability testing to accelerate intrusions. The framework called ARTEX was published on GitHub in July 2026. It was developed under the pseudonym Autumn 27 for authorized security testing. Criminals and targeted intrusion campaigns began using it within weeks of release.

ARTEX uses a planner agent to break objectives into tasks for worker agents. It records findings in a shared graph and requires little operator input. The framework supports different large language models and the Model Context Protocol. Operators have deployed it alongside VShell, GoPhish, and AdaptixC2 on various infrastructures. Other frameworks include Hephaestus, PentAGI, and HexStrike AI which integrates with Claude Code.

Cisco Talos stated these frameworks are the new reality for modern attackers. They noted that AI can be a force multiplier for defenders too. Talos observed that ARTEX compresses work that previously took skilled teams days. They warned that these tools work at speeds impossible for humans to disrupt. The company emphasized that battle tested incident response plans are now imperative.

VAPOR PANDA targeted over 200 organizations in 14 countries starting October 17, 2026. Storm 0940 targeted 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants after compromising ConnectWise application credentials. Storm 3358 targeted financial organizations in Southeast Asia and is based in Cambodia. Unidentified actors targeted South Korean financial firms and stole code signing certificates. Other victims include government, defense, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, and telecommunications organizations.

These frameworks use open source tools like nmap and nuclei for automation. They leverage services such as Shodan, Censys, and residential proxies for mapping. Some tools use Telegram for control while others use web interfaces. The Volta Infostealer previously showed the precursor to autonomous victim prioritization. Attackers use these tools to find exposed credentials in public GitHub repositories.

Future evolutions will likely include autonomous lateral movement and data exfiltration. Attack chains may culminate in autonomous ransomware activation and data theft. One attacker generated 80,000 requests in 90 minutes using an authorization flaw. The articles leave open whether the complete framework was used in South Korea. They do not specify which specific LLMs are most effective for ARTEX.

Articles.Title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms

stories.Headline: Copper prices slid to near four-month low amid fears of hike in U.S. interest rates, lower demand, especially from AI
stories.Summary:
Global benchmark copper prices dropped to a nearly four-month low on Friday, November 13, 2026. This decline was driven by expectations that the U.S. Federal Reserve will increase interest rates. Lower industrial demand from China and the global technology sector also contributed to the slide. Investors also engaged in profit booking following a previous price rally.

The metal was trading at $13,461.99 per tonne, which is about 1.8% lower than the previous day. This shift follows mid-term elections in the United States that resulted in a divided government. Such a political outcome reduced fears regarding tariffs on refined copper imports. However, a fallout involving Nvidia created new worries about future investments in artificial intelligence.

The Federation of Indian Mineral Industries, known as FIMI, attributed the fall to a stronger U.S. dollar and weak industrial demand. FIMI stated that higher interest rates could increase the cost of the dollar-denominated metal. They noted that while short-term prices will be volatile, the long-term outlook is positive. This optimism is based on the growth of electric vehicles, renewable energy, and power infrastructure.

FIMI suggested that India must encourage domestic mining and processing to improve supply security. They argued that reducing import dependence is essential for the country. While lower prices help consumers by cutting costs, FIMI warned that a long decline might hurt exploration investments. The industry body believes that global mine supply constraints will eventually support prices.

stories.Headline: Now agentic AI can perform complex lab research, and maybe cheaper too
stories.Summary:
Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University introduced a new system called AutoDNA on November 4, 2026. This agentic AI platform was detailed in the journal Nature. It is designed to perform complex laboratory research tasks. The system uses AI agents to replace the roles of human researchers. These agents can manage physical activities independently.

The platform changes how biology labs operate by controlling physical tools. It can command a pipette to move fluids into a beaker or use a thermal cycler to heat tubes. The AI can read fluorescence levels in a reaction and complete entire series of experiments. It also observes, documents, and interprets the resulting data. This allows the lab to plan and work on its own.

The scientists from Shanghai Jiao Tong University are responsible for this development. They presented their findings to show that AI can now move beyond computer screens. They explained that while generative AI only provides digital responses, agentic AI performs physical actions. This shift allows the technology to control equipment outside of a computer. The researchers believe this makes complex lab work possible without constant human guidance.

Articles.Title: Now agentic AI can perform complex lab research, and maybe cheaper too

stories.Headline: Google DeepMind AI agents reduce costs for attacking 1024-bit RSA keys
stories.Summary:
Google DeepMind has announced that AI agents, working under human supervision, found two ways to lower the cost of attacking 1024-bit RSA cryptosystems. The work was done with cryptographers from UC San Diego and Inria, and the results were reported on November 10, 2026. The findings suggest that attacks on legacy RSA-1024 need less computing effort than was previously assumed. The company says the results mainly affect these older systems. The first method concerns digital signatures and padding.

DeepMind found that if an attacker controls roughly half or more of a signed block, the padding gives no protection. The finding is especially relevant to the PKCS#1 v1.5 format used in devices such as hardware security modules. In a sandboxed test, the agents re-ran an earlier academic forgery attack on a 1024-bit key and cut the CPU time from 1,380 core-years to 391 core-years, a 3.5-fold improvement. Kohli, VP at Google DeepMind, noted that this signature attack does not recover the private key and requires around 4 billion signing queries made in advance.

The second method concerns factoring several RSA keys of the same size. The agents developed an algorithm that, on average, makes factoring each additional 1024-bit key about 30 times cheaper than previous methods. That estimate, however, assumes an initial computation as costly as factoring one key, and the method has not yet been implemented. Kohli stated that modern encryption protocols, which almost universally use 2048-bit or larger keys, remain secure.

The researchers concluded that cryptographic hardness cannot be treated as a fixed assumption in an era of AI-enabled computation. The researchers emphasised that using AI to rigorously test long-held assumptions will help ensure the security of modern encryption. The articles do not say what steps are planned for operators of legacy 1024-bit systems. More to follow.

Articles.Title: Google DeepMind’s AI Agents Make 1024-Bit RSA Keys Cheaper to Attack - SecurityWeek
